body: The charm is gone. Busy. Beach beds you MUST take off. Constantly several boats docking on an already narrow strip of beach.
title: Overrated

body: This place is so overrated. A small stretch of beach that is overcrowded, noisy and a bit of a tricky climb down a very rocky track.If you want a beach with a load of tourists doing their best poses for Instagram, and boats tied up in the swimming area then fill your boots!
title: Overrated, overcrowded and over it!

body: A great little bay, suitable shallow waters without waves for our one year old grandsons and small girls. Two different cafes, serving reasonable food and excellent Pina Coladas! Get there by Tuk tuk from Galle
title: A great bay for families. Don't get dropped off at the Japanese temple or you climb over rocks to get to 2nd bay!

body: Better atmosphere than in Unawatuna main beach. No litter, cheaper sun beds and less busy .
title: Beautiful, smaller beach

body: Disgusting rubbish piled up all along this small beach and the water was full of it too ... avoid it and travel further down the coast for a less polluted beach experience
title: Rubbish piled up all along the beach

body: From Unawatuna, this beach can be reached either by tuk-tuk or on foot. When you walk through the jungle, you comfort yourself with the hope of being on something so desolate and feeling like Robinson Crusoe. However, such an obvious thought will not only visit you, and upon arrival you will find that there are fewer people here than on the beach of Unawatuna, but their concentration is significantly higher, as the beach is small and narrow. Significantly less than in Unawatuna. There are, you might say, two. So behind the loneliness, definitely not here! But of course, there are benefits. The wave here to the beach is tangent, so it's quiet. Plus, of course, the mangrove jungle adjacent to the beach creates a different atmosphere. Overall, a great addition to Unawatuna Beach, though not an alternative.
title: Being lonely is definitely not here.

body: Jungle Beach in Sri Lanka is a hidden, serene cove near Unawatuna, surrounded by lush forest and calm turquoise water. It’s perfect for swimming, snorkelling, and relaxing away from crowds. The soft sand, coral patches, and peaceful atmosphere make it a favourite spot for travellers seeking nature and quiet coastal beauty.
title: Jungle Beach must visit

body: Jungle Beach Ahungalla is a serene tropical hideaway that perfectly blends nature and comfort. Nestled between lush greenery and the ocean, it offers a peaceful escape from the crowds while still being close to Ahungalla’s beautiful beaches. The rooms are spacious, clean, and designed with a rustic, eco-friendly charm that fits the jungle setting.
title: Amazing place.

body: Jungle beach I think it’s one of the best beaches in sirlanka we went there and we really liked the water and sand and everything was good but there is a lot of people
title: Beautiful beach

body: Lots of plastic waste, sunbeds free, but one drink per person. Sweep only the beach in front of the loungers, otherwise dirty
title: Very sad

body: The calm, clear waters make it ideal for both novice and seasoned swimmers. Underwater, you’ll encounter colorful reef fish, crabs, eels, and occasionally turtles—even if parts of the reef aren’t as vibrant anymoreSome boat tours and snorkeling trips are available too
title: ** Crystal-clear swimming & snorkeling**

body: This beach is in a beautiful setting, surrounded by lush greenery with a beautiful peace pagoda at the top of the path. On the day we visited there was very little sand and the beach was very crowded. The sea is quite rough here so you need to be careful not to swim out too far because of the strong currents, but we loved having fun in the waves. As with lots of other places in Sri Lanka, unfortunately it’s not the cleanest with noticeable plastic rubbish around.
title: Beautiful (and busy) small beach with fun waves

body: Sea full of plastic 😢 The Road to jungle beach is filled with rubbish. More plastic than trees, which all ends up in the sea
title: Plastic soup

body: If you are looking for a truly special beach experience near Unawatuna, this beach promises both a secluded atmosphere and an adventurous approach. It isn’t easy to reach, the most practical way is by tuk tuk, but even then, a steep, winding path leads you down through jungle. The Jungle Beach is a small, picturesque section of coast, where usually there are only a few people, there are no long promenades or big crowds here. Sometimes, loud barking or noisier tourists disturb the peace, but the beach is still popular for its gentle stray dogs who love to lie beside sunbathers, and the monkeys jumping along the path. There are one or two simple cafés on the beach, where you quickly get your refreshments and can also rent a sunbed.
title: Hidden paradise near Unawatuna

body: Overpriced sun loungers. Avoid or bargain harder than me lol. Lots of plastic debris in the sea. Nice enough but overall the plastic trash put me off. It’s actually cleaner than a lot of beaches in SL that we’ve seen so make of that what you will.
title: Nice enough but a little scruffy. Plastic trash in the water. Would I go again? No.

body: Due to the local mafia knock-knock, your tucker will drop you well before entering the location 0.5-1 km). There's a lot of greenery, and really it's like the jungle, you can find monkeys and a lot of natives that frolic in the lagoon on the cramped, because of the people, boats and chaiselongs, beach. We'll have to go back for the road, in a local Rosario Agro three-wheeler.
title: Tropical hell.

body: In this climate with this heat, unbelievably you're not allowed to take your own drinking water or electrolyte water. They check your bags at reception and are not allowed to take any drinks or snacks inside the premises.Totally bizarre… I arrived early and the security man wasn't there, a lady checked my bag, I thought she was just checking for alcohol which might've made sense, I don't drink alcohol. So luckily my first and only visit(I would never go back to a premises with incredibly unhealthy rules like this) I did have my own sports water bottles with me.However knowing as having been a little bit sick recently I need to drink quite a few litres of water per day at the moment, asked for a 1 L of water to mix my electrolytes sachet… They sell only fancy 650 mL glass bottles of water. At extortionate prices I might add. They said it was because their policy was no plastic, it's because they want to charge extortionate prices. Totally agree with cutting down on plastic, and there are ways… but can not their policy of jeopardising peoples hydration health.It isn't a 'swimming pool' per se, if you are looking for a fitness swim this is not the right place it's a play pool, and the establishment is for drinking and partying only. Nothing wrong with that by the way I'm just stating in case others are expecting to go there and have a good swim… You can't.Beautiful setting, lovely beach stunning sea, actually quite nice stuff ... but the whole experience spoilt by lack of care and consideration of health.
title: You cannot take your own drinking water

body: I guess this beach once was beautiful, but it definitely isn’t anymore. Dirty and full of worn-out sunbeds.
title: Find yourself another beach

body: We had higher expectations on this beach. Lots of people and mostly Russians. We chose to leave immediately and find a cozier beach in Unawatuna.
title: Not worth a visit

body: Actually, this beach has everything a "dream beach" would need. Unfortunately, it is quite crowded, the loungers dirty and broken and there is an incredible amount of garbage lying around. It's such a shame. There are also no toilets...
title: Actually nice, BUT...

body: The beach is like a beach, a lot of people on top of each other, a lot of locals. It's not clear why we ended up going there on purpose, we stayed there for an hour and left, nothing special.
title: Visits to the beach

body: We were there at the beginning of February during the week and arrived after the 10 min. Descent to Jungle Beach immediately reversed and walked up again. The beach was completely crowded and packed with beach chairs and restaurants. The view from the beach is not nice either. We like it more idyllic and quiet!
title: Completely overrun and delivered!

body: Finaly is a beach where I can swim!Not waves!Clear wather!Nice walking down!Not croweded,only some people,really like a lot!
title: Nice hidden beach

body: Just a really beautiful place, definitely worth the visit. The Tuk Tuk drivers will not take you up the hill to the beach unless they are the local drivers - so it makes it a bit difficult to get to. But it is worth the effort. The beach has plenty of tourists and locals and you can take tours from the beach as well. There are restaurants and places to buy drinks etc at the beaches. They are small beautiful beaches and swimming in the ocean here is good for all ages. It is ok for snorkelling but no coral, there are a fair few fish. Potentially the snorkelling tours are better. The Japanese Peace Temple is just above the beach and worth a side trip for a quick visit - ignore the pushy caretaker.
title: Beautiful day at Jungle Beach

body: Nice beach. Diverse their holidays at the resort. There were waves on the turtle beach and we went to this one. We took a tuk-tuk for 650 rupees. We met monkeys on the way down to the beach. There are two cafes with sun loungers on the beach. We're set up on blue deckchairs. Freshies were ordered, brought in very quickly. Waves on the beach were minimal. During the lunch we ordered at the same cafe began to descend en masse on the lower branches of the monkey. It was pretty interesting. After lunch, the weather started to deteriorate, a little rain came and waves started to rise. Towards the end of the evening, huge black clouds began to move to the left, thunder rattled and lightning shone. Everyone went home en masse. Back to Unawatuna Beach, we were taken by the cafe guys on a Rs 10,000 boat. It was very exciting and interesting to sail the waves in a motorboat. Had a great time.
title: Great beach

body: Were on this beach, the descent is very steep, through the forest. The beach is clean relatively, the water is clear, there are practically no waves, there is a cafe, sun loungers, at the end of the beach there are many monkeys, you can feed, but they are better off taking food with them. We went there with a local guide, named Eranda, we met on the street, he drives a knock knock, so he and I started rolling all over the beaches. Never been late, never failed, honest and decent, I recommend. We were with him at many locations around the place, and he also took us shopping in Gali, went everywhere with us and tried to help us as much as possible. Very nice to talk to. Highly recommended if you are in unawatun . Number below , contact it will help +94 76 630 9441
title: Jungle beach

body: Relaxed in Hikaduva and decided to change the location a little, remembered Jangle beach, which was well spoken of by acquaintances, took a knock-knock and got to this "wonderful" place, of course I will immediately say that our mistake was to go there on a weekend, so this place is in demand from the local population, so instead of joining nature got the local Gelendzhik , the people were well very many we did not even try swimming. The place itself without people might be called interesting, but the amount of garbage does not allow it. The only plus is a couple of picturesque spots on the way to the beach.
title: I don't recommend wasting time.

body: It consists of a small (closer to Unawatuna) and a large beach (towards Halle), separated by a rocky shore near which constantly swim with masks, and on the very shore on huge sharp-angle boulders climb both ways tourists. The small beach through is too crowded, because it is preferred for swimming, it has no coral reefs (as on the big one), no waves and a very smooth entrance, which is suitable for children. The large beach is much wider and sparsely populated, the beach is just as beautiful and you can lie in the shade of trees. Monkeys at every turn - bring bananas and get plenty of close-range shots.
title: The place is interesting as a one-off walk along picturesque trails and a way to photograph monkeys.

body: Make sure you take the route with the stairs down to the beach! We took the shortcut there and that was a mistake-quite slippery and unpleasant. The beach was lovely but some plastic bottles and unfortunately noise pollution from barking dog and some tourists who don’t respect others - vaping and listening to their videos loudly. Nice for a swim and some monkeys around but would rate this beach too highly.
title: Okay Vibe

body: Beach is good. It’s a five minute walk down hill through a jungle. There are no public toilets or changing rooms at the beach.I would recommend not to litter and take it back to keep the place pristine.If you need to change and have shower a private resident is providing for a small fee. Shower 100 rupees Toilet. 50 rupees
title: Jungle Beach and Public Toilets and Showers

body: We walked from Unawatuna. The road is not very well kept, and I thought it was going to be nicer, more in the jungle. Between the first beach and the other 2 there is a path of large stones, not suitable for little balance. I preferred to swim. And the smallest one, the last one, that doesn't have hammocks... Lovely. White sand, fine, water that changes color, and without much current. You have time, go.
title: Jungle beach, a good place for a calm water bath, away from noise

body: This is the worst place in Sri Lanka. Don't even think about going in there.Terrible road to go down to the beach., Mountains of garbage everywhere on the road and in the sea.People who write positive reviews about this beach, are you even normal? Do you also live in mud and garbage at home?

body: I would like to express my opinion on the famous Sri Lankan Jungle beach. Of all the popular and beautiful things, only monkeys. The ocean looks like a swamp in a village, green, floating around you in mud, garbage, bags, etc. People are lying rough on top of each other. There are locker rooms, but no floors or doors. There is also a small cafe with the service of providing a sunbed, As there are prices and taste I can't say, did not come in. Otherwise, I didn't like it. From the hotels that are nearby, it is a long way to the beach, as they write on rocks and sandbags. According to the campers there, they go to the central beach of unavatuna, a trip to tuk tuk there costs 1,000 rupees, because the road is mountainous. In general, I do not advise, to come swimming I would not, but live, especially.Be careful who plans to get to the kuk tuk you are likely to be brought to the wrong place.There is another place with the same name, but there is purely a restaurant “blue white” to which the same descent.
title: Village Marsh

body: I DO NOT RECOMMEND COMING TO THIS BEACH AT ALL, succinct, full of plastic and disgusting, the bathroom is disgusting you bathe among plastic. SRI lanka has much better beaches. I don't put a zero on it because you can't
title: Very dirty beach

body: Really wanted to watch the famous Jungle Beach. They came to the beach on a tuk tuk. Then a little way down the path and there it is - the beach. The beach has a cafe with sunbeds, no big waves, people swimming. But we didn't go swimming. Very dirty, garbage everywhere, coconut scraps, tree branches. The beach is not looked after at all. Polluting nature, it's all messed up. Near Jungle Beach many monkeys fed them bananas.Back went on foot to Unawatuna to the beach through the forest along a path. You can't get lost, there are signs everywhere. If you turn right and go down the path to the sea, you'll have a small waterfall. And they saw iguanas, peacocks on the way. It took 30 minutes. If the Lankans don't take care of the beach, then let's start with ourselves and not throw rubbish underfoot. Let's not pollute nature, we all live on this little planet!
title: The beach was disappointing.

body: Really disappointing we walked in the jungle surrounded by plastic and when we finally reach the beach, unloaded open waste everywhere that the current brings back. We talk to the owner of the restaurant who tells us that this is very rare and that it comes from the coast and that they are picking up. We find it very sad that such a beautiful piece of paradise and such a beautiful country like Sri Lanka is buried everywhere by garbage. This is the big black spot of our trip with stray dogs covered in fleas...
title: Dirty open-air garbage dump... really sad for nature...

body: We visited Jungle Beach in early September, during the off-season. Initially, we were hesitant because we had read on TripAdvisor that the beach could be overcrowded and littered with garbage. However, our experience was quite the opposite. The beach was clean, the water was calm and perfect for swimming, and we practically had the place to ourselves.The beach bar was closed, which added to the tranquility. Jungle Beach is fairly small, so I can imagine it being quite crowded during the high season. The walk to the beach is about 10 minutes downhill from the car or tuk-tuk park, and it’s important to note that the beach is not wheelchair accessible.
title: Nice tranquil beach in off-season

body: Jungle Beach would be very pretty if it wasn't for the huge amount of rubbish everywhere. It's all we could focus on. Piles of it under the trees at the back of the beach, scattered through the rocks and in the water, so sad to see such a beautiful place spoiled by careless people who don't look after the environment.

body: A small, nice beach in the south with clean water. There is a bar nearby, and it's possible to walk there in about 5 minutes from the car park.

There is a cafe at the beach but it seemed they were packing it up to close for the pending wet season. Staff at the beach cafe were friendly and drinks and snacks were available.Water was calm for swimming but we did observe a young boy who couldn’t swim get into difficulty and his father jump in fully dressed to save him. Took a tuk tuk from Galle Fort for 500LKR but the return trip was 1500LKR . There will be a few drivers waiting for your return fare.Happy we visited Jungle Beach despite some of the negative reviews.

body: Idyllic beach with free sunbeds and brollies if you buy a drink or eat at the cafe. There is a row of coral pieces to walk through between the sand of the beach and the sand in the sea but is fine if you tread cautiously. We had so much fun swimming and bouncing in the sea.There are a few beautiful fish to see snorkeling however the coral is dull and for us, it wasn't worth snorkeling more than once.The huge benefit to a fifty something lady is a clean, nice smelling and flushing toilet, although I recommend bringing tissues and the torch on your phone as there is no light.It can get quite busy so we always went in the morning.Best to take a tuk tuk to the jungle beach path unless you are very fit as the road is steep and endlessly uphill...even the tuk tuks struggle...The path to jungle beach is full of ups and downs, twists and turns, with some slippery places...watch out for over hanging branches as I clonked my head! Not for those with limited mobility/balance.We visited 3 times and far preferred it to the more touristy/hotel-laden Unawatuna beach.
title: Our favourite beach near Unawatuna

body: If you want to go to Sri Lanka with children, then choose this place - here the ocean is calmer, the infrastructure is developed, there is a choice of food to suit your taste and there are more opportunities to relax.

body: It probably was a beautiful beach once but it is now crowded with people and dirty. There’s not even a spot to sit and even less a spot to swim. We went there on a weekend so there were many locals in addition to the tourists and it was fully packed.
title: Fully packed and dirty

body: Loved our stay here. The hotel has lovely rooms that look out over the sea. From the roof terrace you can see amazing sunsets. A fairly stiff uneven walk of 10 minutes take you down to a paradise beach that is safe and so beautiful. The owners son is a qualified life guard and invited me to go snorkelling with him around the headland. It was an unforgettable experience and I’m so grateful for the kindness he showed to my wife and I. Nothing was too much trouble. If you like nature you’ll love Jungle Beach.
title: A wonderful place for nature lovers

body: Lovely beach surrounded by natural beauty, as the name suggests you have to do a trick to get there so would not be for everyone but if you are able to make a visit. There in August so sea us quite choppy but still stunning
title: Great beach

body: We spent 4 nights here as part of a road trip around Sri Lanka with our 2 teenage children (16 & 18) It has a stunning location and we swam in the sea and the pool every day. The staff were very friendly, in particular the bar tended who made us some fantastic cocktails every evening. The restaurant was beautiful and the food was very good, however, we found that the quantity was just too much. We were brought automatically brought an enormous tray of pastries (at least 4 each) yogurt, smoothies and lots of fruit. we were then expected to order from the (very extensive a la carte menu) we saw so much food left on tables. The evening menu was then 3 or 4 courses! Again we saw so much food wasted. Housekeeping came around 4 times a day to clean, change towels, turn down the beds and bring snacks!! If you have an enormous appetite you will love it. But for us, it was a bit too much. When we asked for our beds not to be changed as we were leaving the following morning, they still changed them and made us feel a bit ridiculous to have asked. Overall though we had a great and relaxing time!
title: A great place to visit.

body: Just a little beach but hassle 2 get 2 but no monkeys as they only come in morning and late afternoon but it was a nice swim
title: Not a bad morning swim

Just ignore that and try to enjoy the remaining natural beauty.(Beach near to forest - interesting)As a Local I think it's good to bring your food and essentials from outside the beach because the prices are high than usual.

body: nice beach i went with my friends. it is calm and quite beach you have to go through jungle to the beach its little duty but still can enjoy

body: A hidden gem off the coast of Sri Lanka, this bay is perfect for a dip in the ocean as there are no waves! You need to go as far as possible by vehicle down the unawatuna stretch and find parking (usually at a guest house for a nominal fee) and then it’s a short trek (approx 15 - 20 mins) from there. (We had a group of 8 kids aged 7-12). Pack a towel, change of clothes, sun block & a picnic. No changing rooms so use a sarong / towel as a make shift cover :) There are a few stalls selling juice, snacks and water (sign posted in English and Russian!) en route but I’m not sure of prices. The achcharu at the stall down at the bay (at jungle beach) was reasonably priced. It is a famous spot so expect a crowd but also just ignore and make it your own. Some other reviewers complain about “too many locals” - this is our island and we welcome all, equally. Please don’t expect us to refrain from enjoying our own island! There were also comments that it was dirty - we didn’t witness any trash on the beach. It was a little crowded but not to the extent that we couldn’t find a spot. There were some people cooking a meal on a rock close by but it didn’t seem to bother the crowd and we didn’t see any litter. Soak in the sun and sea (while getting ready for the trek back to the vehicle - the only downside!)
title: Beautiful bay to soak up the Sun & Sea

body: terribly dirty beach with full of locals .Actually among the greatest beahes in Sri Lanka this one was the worst .the jungle road was even not the easiest to reach .doesnt worth an effort

body: Nice beach for a sea bath. You need to park the vehicle and move little bit . But it is worth the travel. It is getting crowded during the evening

Not to mention the army of stray dogs and cats everywhere. Our view is srilanka is rapidly becoming paradise lostIs it do difficult to educate children and adults to not litter and to keep their heritage clean.Apart from that you get some good photos because the jungle touches the beach at this point.

body: We went to Unawatuna for three days just to end our holidays on the beach. This was beginning of August. Everyone said that it was better not to go because of the raining seasin but we saw really a little bit of rain. Unawatuna is a niice place close to Galle where we went around the fort. We realy liked to stay there even when it was not the season to be there for surfing or diving.

body: Unfortunately was this beach full of trash and not really inviting to spend much time there! 😔 really sorry to see such things happening to the nature!

body: This Hidden lovely beach is few kilomitrs away from Unawatuna Beach. Its Located near to small forest and you have to walk to this hidden Beach. Its less Crowded and so senic. Sunset is amazing. There is parking facilities and better to come back from forest after 6.30 PM.
