body: Go to the Jungle beach cafe which is the first place you pull up to at Jungle beach if getting dropped by Rick. Have a nice chicken and cheese omlette, and go and take amazing pictures on their terrace. Find Pasindu and he will take you around and ask to be introduced to his brother if you are looking to have a local legend teach you how to scuba dive. He didn't even speak a word about cost- just said pay what you feel like after. He just has a love for scuba and i got lucky. He takes his time and shows you some awesome spots as well as picks out litter from the sea along the way (amazing person) you have to meet the brothers!
title: Brilliant Beach for Scuba and Pictures!

body: Actually two beaches. The main larger Jungle beach is accessed by a steep in part, stepped in other parts, quite uneven rocky ground from the car park of the same name on the Rumasalla road. A good stretch of curving sandy beach with one beach bar with a few sunbeds. Busy on National Day with locals but quite quiet another. A very pretty cove with stunning water colour, good swimming with no waves. Around the coast, 200 metres of large rocks to clamber over is the smaller beach. Still very picturesque, just smaller. This can also be accessed from the car park on google maps next to the Peace Pagoda and has a less steep walk to it that the larger jungle beach.
title: Two Jungle beaches next to each other

body: The beach itself and all the greenery is magical. Getting there, not so. If you are scared of step down hill, or have trouble walking uphill, this place is not for you. When I went, there was a large number of people and unfortunately not enough space if it were to get more packed. There is a small juice bar but while watching the man make my drink, I just knew I was going to catch something. Not from him necessarily, but from the extreme lack of food hygiene. After my drink I decided to take a boat with a guy named LARA who I found out later was well known for all the wrong reasons, so beware! He is a not honest. And he has very creepy looks. He tried to charge me 20,000 LKR for less than an hour of a boat ride with no stop to see anything. With all the other beaches around Sri Lanka, I would definitely put a pass on this one. I wouldn't consider it a MUST see.
title: Beautiful beach but not worth the trouble

body: Jungle beach is rather pleasant once you get there.Access is via a mountain path that is medium long, rocky and uneven and whilst the agile and fit can negotiate it with ease it is difficult for most of us over 70 - as I am.There is a nice shack on the beach that serves decent food at reasonable prices.The water is fresh and clear, the beach nice clean and good sand.When it came to leave I was told that the easiest route was to walk along the sea path back to Unawatuna. I was also told it would take me 5-10 min.How wrong was this info. I am sure a mountain goat could have negotiated the uneven and loose boulders far better than my arthritic sloth like agility, the boulders are rather hazardous but eventually you come to another beach. Then you have to climb back up the mountain !!Bad choice should have gone up the way I went down.However the beach is nice, what would be nice is a boat taxi running at regular intervals from Unawatuna to all these small beaches, when and if this occurs I will go back but until then leave it to those who are more agile.
title: Lovely beach but not for those of us who are older as access is difficult

body: Unawatuna Jungle Beach is one of the most fascinating beaches near the Galle- Unawatuna area. Small woods and beautiful trees give an eye-catching view to the beach.There are two sides which hava e proper beach in this area and you can go from one another through an adventurous small route stepping on rocks.You can take a three-wheel (tuk) or a bike to go close to this beach but the road is full of hills. If you are going on a bicycle motorbike be extremely careful with your breaks because when you come back steeps are extremely dangerous and there were a lot of accidents.
title: Fabulous Beach through a dangerous hilly road.

body: This place is incredible if you go on a Sunday, because it will be filled wiith local people who go to the sea with friends and family, so there is a charming atmosphere: many different people enjoying their incredible sea in a local way, which is the vibe I love to discover and join when I travel. The little bay is lovely, you can rent sunbeds and there is a small cafè that serves good food and cold drinks, beers and cocktails too, at honest price seen the place, that is very difficoult to reach. You will have to follow a steep path from the main road -where you leave your transport mean- down to the sea level and it’s not advisable for people who have a walking problem, beacuse it’s not paved and in some parts there are slippery passages on rocks. Coming up will be a bit heavy, but it’s surely worth the effort. Go and visit the nearby temple too, Peace Pagoda, bcause it’s very close and it’s a great place for the soul and for the landscapes you can enjoy from its first floor.
title: Quaint and lovely

body: If you want to make your mind relax this is the place for it. One of the beautiful beach in the world.Longest Coral line in South Asia.Valuable jungle Sunset/ sun bath.
title: Clear Beach

body: Not easy to access , however worth the hike ! We took a boat from Jungle beach back to Unawatuna which was also amazing view. At the bech there is a small bar serving cold drinks but nothing more than this is available
title: Great beach

body: This beach requires you to walk through the jungle, hence the name, till you get to the beach. Go early so it's not too crowded, find a spot and relax. You can get food/drinks from the shack, swim, snorkel or just relax. Leave in time, going back up at sunset isn't the safest.
title: Definitely visit!

body: Jungle Beach is a small bay surrounded by jungle located in Rumassala, northwest of Unawatuna where you can enjoy a great day of sunbathing and snorkeling.Anyone with snorkeling gear can walk out and enjoy life on the reef.Things to do in Jungle BeachWalk along the beachSnorkelingVisit Japanese Peace PagodaSwim in the seaWatch Sunset
title: Enjoy a great day of sunbathing and snorkeling

body: We were expecting a little bit more out of our visit to Jungle Beach in Unuwatuna. The beach is littered with plastic and debris left behind from mindless locals and tourists alike. It is unfortunate as the beach could be beautiful if cleaned up and maintained better.
title: Plastic Beach

body: Jungle beach it’s nice and calm beach enjoy your holiday possible visit Japanese temple good place to Snorkaling
title: Good place to visit

body: We went to Jungle beach, both of them. Recommended in loney planet. But it is so dirty, nothing to see underwater and you dont even want to go into the water because there is so much plastic and face masks and everything in the water. Also on the beach as you can see on the pictures. The wild life seems to adapt a little ( se picture)
title: The “secret beach”, keep it that way !!

body: The walk there is cool and should be combined with peace pagoda, then once there its really junglish and cool - but oh so dirty. No fun to swim with the dirt. Note that the bar on the beach is closed since covid and has been reclaimed by nature.
title: Great setting - but I hope they clean it

body: This is how a beach should be... just so beautiful. The only thing I don't like is that you will go there and I am greedy and want it all to myself! :-)
title: I felt like I was in a James Bond film!

body: Jungle Beach is a nice place to have a sea bath. Clear water & less crowded, may be because we visited on a week day.
title: Nice place to have a sea bath

body: Really nice natural beach. About 20 minute walk from central Unawatuna through the forest. Less commercialised then the other beaches.
title: Lovely beach

body: Nice beach for a sea bath. You need to park the vehicle and move little bit . But it is worth the travel.
title: Excellent

body: Highly recommend for a adventure seekers. Also, it's good for a safe swimming. We went there in the afternoon as it was a sudden plan. On our way only we decided to do some outdoor cooking just for a change. Before you enter the location, you can enjoy cool king coconut from the street sellers. You can do some out door cooking in the beach with limited resources. But you have protect your belongings from Monkeys. Best time to head back is on or before 18:30Hrs as it's dark during that time. Please make sure to leave only your foot prints when you go back.
title: Outdoor Cooking in the Sandy Beach

body: Jungle beach is a whitish sandy beach surrounded by a jungle situated at Rumassala-Galle. This was the watering point of ships of old silk route. There are foot pathways from Bonavista road to jungle beach. As this place is popular among locals better visit on a weekday.
title: Whitish sandy beach surrounded by jungle

body: The place is good for safe swimming, but bit rough though. Coral reef cut off the strong waves. But, standing on shore can be bit harsh for the feet since sand full of pieces of coral. Those pieces of comes with the fast waves.Sadly at the time I visit this valuable piece of land mass has been full of plastic bottles and waste. Sri Lanka Navy and locals known to clean the entire area periodically, but it's completely visitors responsibility not to ruin the place.
title: Surrounding area is good

body: Nice beach, if a bit small. Better for swimming than the surfing beaches near town. Very popular and lots of people. There's a bit of walk down to the water.
title: Nice but small swimming beach

body: Completely overrated. View of the bay and port of Galle/factories in the distance.far better beaches in SL
title: Dont Bother.

body: This beach literally is between a jungle as shown in the picture, its very cool and relaxing but very crowded as you have to go so early if you want a good place sit, i recommend not to go in any weekend or local vacation to avoid crowding.
title: Very relaxing beach 😍

body: Nice place. This time we had the beach for ourselves. Its a bit like jungle and private.. Really liked it.
title: Nice beach

body: Went here as had read great TA reviews. Very crowded - Need to be there very early if you want a sun-bed. Small eatery which was ok (and who I think own the sun beds). To be honest we went to better beaches in the area. Wijaya was much nicer with lovely restaurant.
title: Overrated

body: Less than expected. Nothing special. Better go to Mirissa and visit Secret beach, which is more spectacular.
title: Nothing special

body: It takes quite an effort to reach here. You have to pass through a path full of rocks and greenery. So wear comfortable shoes if you are planning to visit this place.The effort of reaching looks fruitful once you reach the beach. The water is crystal clear and its not much crowded. A small beach but a must visit if you are visiting Galle or unnawatuna. We came here on a day trip from Bentota
title: A must visit Beach

body: We walked to Jungle beach from Unawatuna in about an hour, through trees,it was lovely.If you are feeling less energetic you can get a tuk tuk for about 500 rupees.The beach does get quite busy but there is a small juice bar and glass bottom boat and feeding the monkeys is fun.
title: Beautiful and secluded

body: just a one & half hours away from Colombo via the southern expressway, just a few kilometers away from the highway exit Pinnaduwa, you can go with your own food or buy your food from nearby locals. mainly there are two places that provide parking space for vehicles we went to the second one that comes after the peak point in the downward which have an 'L' turn to the right. you can park vehicles, have a shower and some good food you can enjoy.
title: A great beach

body: It's definitely worth the way if you are looking for that Paradise beach experience. Actually, from Unawatuna center ist just 5 min of tuktuk and 10 min walking. You can do it! There is a great view on the galle bay, clear water, the beach kisses the jungle and palmtrees all around it. Not crowded at all and locals also like to go there a lot. Stop by at Agnus Villa next door for a sunset drink on the rooftop for the most amazing view you can imagine
title: Best beach in the area

body: There is a beautiful view of the Galle city, a lovely bar, but if a boat will starts its engine to go to Galle, you cannot breathe.
title: Too much pollution from the boats

body: This is a nice beach but not maintained properly. The access to the beach is through a jungle. If some efforts can be taken this will become a awesome experience.
title: Nice beach

body: It could be a beautiful little beach with a stunning jungle walk to reach it, but once we arrived I was disappointed with how busy it was, there’s was no room to lay on the beach, large crowds of tours and extremely loud. Not peaceful as I envisioned
title: To crowded

body: Smaller and more remote than the other beaches in the area check it out for more private swim time (though avoid Saturdays when throngs of locals are likely to come).
title: More Remote

body: Lots of people, lots of trash everywhere, noisy. Really not a place you want to spend your time at if you want to relax...
title: Dirty, crowded, terrible!

body: The jungle beach is quite crowded but the small path to walk there is very beautiful through the jungle and with some viewpoints.
title: Quite busy

body: The beach itself is really nice and beautiful. But there is a lot of trash everywhere! We really couldn't understand the amount of emply water bottles and plastic bags. Way down from the road to the beach is a bit difficult, I had troubles with my flipflops.
title: Nice beach

body: The view of the sea is fabulous. Shorts above the knee are not allowed. Although they give a piece of cloth to cover up. The drive up to this place is very nice. The various stages of Buddha’s life are also well explained and shown. A must visit place if you are around Galle.
title: A beautiful and serene place.

body: Short walk through the jungle to get there. It was busy when we arrived but it’s worth a visit. Water is calmer here than Dalawella beach so you can to for a swim.
title: Beautiful beach

body: There are guys selling cold beer and coconuts on the shore we loved this beach. We stand up paddled here which was awesome, then snorkeled for a bit before having a cold beer and chilling on the sand, the beach it a popular attraction and it was pretty busy.
title: White sand, clear water

body: This beach is was the dirtiest beach I’ve seen not only in Sri Lanka, but also in my all Asia trips I’ve been making for 12 years. Even the view is veautiful at beach, we couldn’t swim well because the water is rocky. Furthermore, you shoul climb too many steps to back from the beach. For me, you should skip this beach if you are into swimmable beaches.
title: Very dirty

body: Nice beach but heavily littered and dirty. Too crowded on a regular weekday. Expected far more. Not worth to take the climb down/up
title: Crowded and dirty

body: The beach is kids friendly (opposite many other beaches nearby) but the down side is that it’s difficult to reach with small children. There are two bars at the beach.
title: Nice secluded Beach with shadow

body: A fantastic beach yards from the "jungle". Well worth the walk from where the Tuk Tuk driver drops you. Small beach so get there early.
title: Picture perfect

body: Very nice beach but on the weekend is crowded with locals so looks nothing like the pictures. We walked from Unawatuna beach via the Japanese Peace Pagoda which was a nice walk and then a tuk tuk back to Unawatuna.
title: Pretty beach but do not visit on the weekend

body: Jungle beach must have been a breathtaking sight a long time back. But unfortunately not anymore. After a perilous trek through the jungle and over the rock from one beach to another, it was an utter disappointment to find the second beach was to be as overcrowded and unattractive as the first.After somehow managing to get a spot for ourselves to sit on the beach and a couple of hours later, a fight broke out between some beachgoers and some beach boys. One beachgoer got himself floored by a beach thug and his buddies had to literally carry him away. It was scary and apparent that these areas were under these thugs' "jurisdiction".If i could help it, I will visit jungle beach never again.
title: Beach thugs

body: Simply put, a beautiful beach, with beautiful views, nice bathing and stunning views, with a great vibe. Very clean, although it takes a bit of effort to clamber down and then back up a rough pathway.
title: Natural Beauty

body: We enjoyed the challenge of walking to jungle beach and climbing over the rocks.Once there it was a nice little bay to swim and relax.There is a stall selling drinks and beer and a resturant at the top if you want something to eat.
title: Worth the effort

body: Amazing intact beach. Problem with baby jelly stings. Nice fish appreciated when snorkeling. Coconut trees
title: Amazing intact beach.

body: Very nice Sri Lankan Rice & Curry. The place has fair prices and it lays just 100 meters away from the main road & beach.
title: Great lunch

body: The place is lesser known. But its a spectacular beach front. One restaurant. A little bit of a walk.
title: Finest Beaches In Unawatuna

body: Yes, it’s is a bit of an adventure to reach (down a steep hill and series of stairs), but that kind of adds to the experience of ‘discovering ‘ Jungle Beach.Apply lots of bug spray for the descent.The beach itself is lovely, although you need to be wary of the sharp coral the has collected as you enter, and several large rocks not far from shore. The cove is protected, so the sea is quite calm, even as the tide comes in and churns it up a bit. The water is extremely warm and it’s relaxing just to float around and enjoy the quiet. We went on a Monday, which meant it was relatively uncrowded. It’s just sad that many people have clearly disregarded the signs to not toss garbage. You can find trash and discarded food all around the edges of the beach.Otherwise, it’s a wonderful spot.
title: Relaxing beach

body: We went her a couple of times. I liked the walk down the uneven path, through the trees with monkeys over head. Lots of locals come here and everyone smiles as you pass. Buy water at the top. Food on the beach is great, we shared a big plate of rice. Boys at the bar are fun. There is only a squat toilet and it don’t smell too good. Lo gets they charge if your not eating. The water has rocks in the middle but you can have a lovely swim here and sit in the shade. We walked round to the next beach watching the locals having fun. Then up the hill to see the temple and could here the ship wreck.
title: Lovely cove and snorkeling a bit cloudy

body: Went there after a visit to the nearby Japanese peace pagoda, but didn't stay more than 5 minutes. The beach was quite dirty, used mostly by locals. Nothing impressive...
title: Dirty and disappointing.

body: This is located about 10 mins away from the main city. 500m away from the Peace Pagoda Rumassala. There is a jungle beach parking lot and the path leads to the beach from there. It about a 15 min trek down to the beach through the jungle. Path is sometimes tricky but there are stone stairways to make it easier. During mid day the place gets pretty crowded. The sea is clam and you can walk a long way into the sea. There is only a single cocktail bar on the beach. Near the parking lot you can drink local king coconut water etc. For those of who want to wash off the salty water there are plenty of local houses which offer a wash off for 50 bucks. From the parking lot, go towards the peace pagoda side and take the first left and you will find plenty of places.
title: Serene waters

body: We chose to go there because it was recommended for snorkeling.There are 2 little beaches,linked between by a pathway parallel with the seashore. It was fully crowded when we get there,at around 4 p.m.We chose the second beach and went snorkel parallel with the shore, towards the end point of the peninsula. That is were the magic happened. Although at first the water was blury, after 10 minutes of swimming we began to see real show. It's crowded with reef fish and corals. So for snorkel it's wondeful, if you know where to look. Otherwise, i wouldn't come here for the beach.
title: Not secret,not secluded,not hard to get to

body: It’s a tough walk through jungle to get here but it is worth it. Nice little beach with a bar serving cocktails at a reasonable price. It’s pretty popular beach with both locals and tourists
title: Secret beach

body: This beach is great. The sea is lovely and calm and excellent for snorkelling. It can get busy so best to arrive quite early. Beer, cocktails etc are available and snorkelling gear can be rented. The neighbouring beach has sun lounges and kayaks for rent and you can order food. We preferred this one as it was less busy.
title: Great beach and snorkelling

body: The beach is nice with a scenic setting. It is about as crowded as the Unawatuna beach. The beach quite clean.
title: Cozy beach

body: This restaurant for me is the best in Unawatuna!! I came here last year and thoroughly enjoyed it. I had chicken satay to start which was awesome then belly pork. It was just fabulous. I finished off with creme bruleu which was just out of this world. It was for two people so my friend helped me, but unfortunately we couldn’t finish it. I wanted to take it back to Wales with me. As it’s our last night in Unawatuna tonight we couldn’t finish our holiday without returning this restaurant. Who knows I might even try something else!! Just fab. We tend to eat early and arrive at this restaurant about 6.45 which we were told to do as it gets extremely busy after that. I believe it closes at 10pm anyway. Sometimes they have to close the gate early as they have so man6 customers still arriving late.Enjoy!!! Well worth it
title: Amazing restaurant

body: overcrowded by locals.. but for a reason... because its an amazing beach with crystal water... We descended to the beach from the pagoda and went back up from the other end. Recommend to go snorkeling..! One of the highlights in my December visit for sure...!
title: Crowded but awesome

body: So many people, not a secret spot anymore. Actually more locals than tourists but still only go if you want to have 'fun'. The nearby Japanese Peace Pagoda is well worth exploring.
title: Way to crowded

body: Jungle beach was a wonderful experience. The short easy stroll down the mountain to the secluded beach. There are locals down on the beach where you can rent a day bed or get a cocktail or beer. There are quite a few monkeys to be seen as well. A very relaxing place
title: Serene

body: This is a place which requires some effort to reach and probably that's why it is so clean and unspoilt. The water is clean and the waves are gentle so good for swimming and playing around. Just that since it is cut off from the town you would need to leave before it gets dark!
title: Beautiful pristine beach

body: Not worth the long sweaty track there. Super crowded beach. Much more beautiful beaches further south west in SL .
title: Crowded

body: A beautiful but VERY small beach!! Don't go there. So many people, a lot of dead corals in the sand, two of us got hurt in our feets when going for a swim. Only one tiny restaurant, they had some sunbeds (very hard in wood) for free of if you ate there, otherwise they wanted 1500 for a bed!!! This is a really tourist trap! There are so many other beautiful beaches, like Habaraduwa for ex.
title: Don't go!!!!!

body: It was a little bit dirty, the people should worried about garbage, the first train was really dirty
title: Not so good

body: We had a lovely walk to the beach from our accommodation through the forest came across monkeys and a monitor lizard on route. The beach was busy as everyone is on holiday on Christmas Eve it’s very small and had two very small stalls selling a few drinks and snacks nothing special as there is no road down to the beach. The walk and temple for us was just as interesting as the beach.
title: A small and lovely beach

body: Beach was very beautiful, much nicer than unawatuna beach. Good for swimming. We also saw monkeys there. Defenetly worth visiting!
title: Beautiful beach

body: This place is way too crowded with people for a very small beach. Also, there's jellyfish in the water.
title: Too crowded and many jellyfish

body: The water at the beach was very murky and there were tons of washed up coral at the beach. Not a nice sandy beach at all and you couldn't see anything in the water. We brought snorkeling gear but sadly couldn't really use it. The walk to the beach is a small hike through a little bit of jungle if you are coming from the unawatuna side, it's not bad but even if you take a tuktuk there is still some way through the jungle. Be aware that once you reach the first small beach you have to walk/climb all the big rocks next to the water in order to reach the next bigger jungle beach. There is no jungle path connecting the two beaches as we thought.Wouldn't go again, if you want to experience this beach then go to Google images as you'll get a better experience there.
title: Dont bother

body: Garbage is everywhere. Beach has lot of corals and stones under water.But nature is still there, trying to be alive.
title: Lot of garbage

body: There were two separate small beatches, which were both very nice. It’s a bit far from the unawatuna beach. Most people go there by tuk tuk, but it’s also possible to walk there, if you like a bit of an exercise.
title: Better than the main beach

body: Quite full beach, but better than main unawatuna beach. A lot of locals here. Service available. Stone walk to the beach.
title: Nothing special but nice

body: One of the pure exotic beaches in galle.We have to take a short trip around 800 meters downwards to reach the beach.It will be like a mini trekking experience with the path is very uneven till 300 meters. And we have a steep downward path will be very hard for the children and older adults.After the 300 meters of intense step path there are steps leading to the beach.One of the exotic peaceful beaches in Galle or Srilanka. It will be good experience for kids and couples to spend time here.
title: Jungle Beach(Exotic Beach)

body: Hidden beach in a cove.. neee get through a small piece of a jungle... white sand beach.. and Clearwater.. just loved it...there was a restaurant which doesn't exist now...
title: Amazing beaches

body: The perfect beach.Safe swimming with life gards.Stayed all after noon.Ideal for adults and children.
title: Really worth a visit

body: Beautiful cove with sandy beach and very calm water. Need to take a short hike along a jungle footpath to reach it.If you walk over the boulders to the left of the cove, there is another cove with a shipwreck. The walk over the boulders is a bit tricky though.
title: Hidden gem

body: A lovely walk down to the beach, quite steep and slippery so definitely don’t wear flip flops.....you need comfy shoes! Went down to the beach where there are two huts for drinks and also sun loungers but the beach is very dirty. Broken glass in the sand, a lot of rubbish and shells everywhere. We walked down for a visit but didn’t stay. Visit unawatuna beach for a more relaxing, clean beach.
title: Ok beach. Nothing special. Quite dirty.

body: hidden beach surrounded by a small jungle after like 10 min trek, nice to have a good sea bath while enjoying the beauty of nature.
title: breathtaking

body: Very cool, It is a hike to get there but it is nice. There are two beaches, jungle white beach and jungle beach. You might need a tuk tuk, bike or taxi to get there.
title: Cool beach

body: Lovely place to visit in jungle beach .The beach itself is hidden away from the business of Unawatuna and was very quiet and peaceful when we went.
title: Lovely place to visit in jungle beach

body: Nice walk over the hill from Unawatuna. Be sure to get some photos of the peace pagoda and the shipwreck on your way to the beach. The ship wreck is located on the rocks between jungle beach and Unawatuna. The beach itself is split in two and either are good for a swim or snorkel. The coral is bleached but still plenty of colourful fish and the water is clean
title: Scenic beach and surrounds

body: A must visit place in South Beach. Very beautiful and nice view. Some times quite busy because both locals and foreigns visit the place.
title: Most beautiful beach in South Coast

body: Lovely place to visit in unawatuna this beach have with jungle When your wanna visit your have to go by foot little distance
title: Beautiful nature

body: Take the tome and enjoy a short walk down to the beach. While there is coral in the water it is still a lovely setting looking back to Galle fort. Lots of vegetation behind and the opportunity to have a cocktail and some food is an option.
title: Relaxing

body: This small beach could be fantastic but unfortunately it has been spoilt by the amount of rubbish surrounding it. It’s such a shame something so simple is ruining this area. There are no bins anywhere on or near the beach and people have left plastic bottles, beer cans, wrappers etc all over the floor which is completely unacceptable! The beach itself is hidden away from the business of Unawatuna and was very quiet and peaceful when we went. Although I’m sure in the peak season it’s extremely busy which may make it difficult to find a spot. It’s very small, especially when the tide is in.
title: Lovely setting but needs a clesn

body: I’m sure this small beach was once very lovely. It is now ruined. There is a large pile of plastic and rubbish about 50m from the beach entrance (and a lot more on the walk through the jungle and at the main road). There is a huge amount of plastic and rubbish in the sea - you get plastic bags wrapped around your legs when you swim. It’s depressing and a bit disgusting. Admittedly it might have been the conditions on the day so I spokeTo the beach bar owner who said shops and people all along the coast are dumping trash into the sea and it winds up on Jungle Beach when the conditions are right, and nobody will help to clean it up.I would avoid this place completely - the tiny beaches around the fort are cleaner and less depressing
title: Paradise lost!

body: It is worth visiting these beaches and its surroundings. Beautiful view, and the path to the beach is already an adventure.
title: Nice place

body: I've visited Sri Lanka three times over the recent years and always make a visit to jungle beach. This time I was shocked and saddened to see how much rubbish and plastic were left on the beach. The locals who work at the beach bar must do something urgently to prevent these plastic bottles and other items from entering the water. I've added photos to show the rubbish tip on jungle beach. This tip was found at the far side of the beach, opposite the beach bar and sun lounges.Furthermore the swimming experience at jungle beach was awful. I stepped on and swam through heaps of plastic bags. The worst part is that I spied a small turtle swimming through this too.Unfortunately it's been raining and storming a lot in galle over past days so plastic from the beach is no doubt being pushed and blown into the waters. Me and my boyfriend tried to take as much rubbish as we could back up with us but there's still tons down there. The locals and tourists who enjoy this beach must be more waste aware and not dispose of their rubbish so carelessly.I would like to add photos however the file sizes are too large and trip advisor only allows 5mb photo uploads.
title: Rubbish tip

body: Beautiful location rich with natural beauty. Have to walk in through a small jungle for about 10 minutes to reach the beach. The sea can be rough during certain days of the month so its important to be extra cautious .
title: One of a kind experience !

body: Started off from Unawatuna beach and passed by a village along the way. Managed to find an old lady selling chilled, fresh coconuts along the way and had a fun conversation. No problems finding the beach there were signs and a well-trodden path when the tarmac gave way to dirt. There’s a small stall selling fresh fruits and drinks there so one should be well-taken care of.However, Tuk-Tuks will be hard to find at the beach’s entrance so you will have to walk out a little bit before you can find one (assuming that you do not want to walk back to your accommodation after a day of chilling by the water).
title: Fun trek to reach the beach.

body: Very good for a nice pic. But it's better to go to unawatuna if you want to go in the water. This beach has a lot of rocks
title: Not too good to swim

body: I visited the beach in the first week of August, found it quiet and very beautiful but was rough for the swim. I enjoyed went down through the jungle and stairs to reach the beach.
title: Enjoyed

body: Jungle beach is one of a beautiful place situated in galle district . Jungle beach is suitable to enjoy swimming without waves . Jungle beach surrounded with a rich bio diversity . Some people say the Rumassala mountain is a part of Himalaya range which was carried by "Hanuman".
title: Enjoy peace and lovely nature

body: Beach is nice for sunset and a bit hidden. You should be careful with the current. Not perfect for a swim, but nice for snorkeling.
title: Sunset

body: A secluded beach, with snorkeling and just a few vendors. Definitely worth a visiting if you have some time in Unawatuna
title: Quiet beautiful beach

body: It was beautiful. But for us not that much to see. We walked arround and that was more Fun! If you go to jungle village hotel you can walk through the hotel and end up in the most beautiful sceneries were locals live
title: Maybe overrated to see

body: Yes, it is really detached. If this is most important to you, go on.On the other hand, you have to go uphill, then downhill by forest path, and the beach is not equipped with showers or umbrellas, only a few sunbeds and single (a sort of) bar with some drinks of questionable quality.
title: Far away and not equipped

body: Just a small beach with lots of palm trees around. Would've enjoyed it if it wasn't for lots of rubbish around.
title: Nothing special

body: My husband and I visited today, I obviously expected there so be some aspect of jungle to this place. However I didn’t anticipate, when putting my sanders on that morning, that I would quite literally be hiking through a jungle to get down to it! The hike isn’t a strenuous one as such but certainly I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone with any mobility issues or anyone prone to falls/being off balance. Especially after a rain storm it can be quite slippery. The beach itself is beautiful and quaint, clean sand, blue sea, a little beach shack and a few sun loungers for chilling. My only criticism is the trash littering the beach, this place could really do with someone taking down a role of trash bags and doing a clean up mission!! Had I known this before I would have done so myself!! But beautiful for relaxing. 1 piece of advise: don’t play with the dog, he got quite nippy and over excited. A rabies jab is not what you want from your trip to jungle beach.
title: The name makes sense

body: Walk to jungle beach is nice, but the beach are pretty messy at the moment with choppy waves, not the best swimming spot for the off season. My tip would be to stay East! Wish we did. Also, lots of rubbish on the second beach! Never very tempting
title: Average at the moment

body: Nice quiet beach with warm water, sheltered from strong ocean waves. Only beach on whole trip where i was able to lie at water and not care about strong waves. Most of the beach is in jungle shade. It was bit crowded, but still OK.
title: Nice quiet beach

body: A 10min trek down a jungle slope (stairs) and you reach a little strip of beach. Soft sand and great waters. There are loungers on the beach that are free, and there is one small bar that serves alcohol and food. Probabky best to bring your own watee and snacks though. Definitely worth a visit! Tuk tuks at the jungle entrance ready to take you back to your hotel.
title: Cosy little hideaway

body: We were disappointed as we wanted to enjoy the sea and a nice beach on our last day in Sri Lanka. But we had to walk a lot in the jungle and when we finally got to the beach, it wasn't what we expected - rocks & waves. We had a child with us and we understood people recommend that beach for kids also - I still don't understand why.I recommend Wijaya instead :) The day before we got to enjoy swimming with giant turtles in Wijaya.
title: It's more about the Jungle and less about the Beach

body: We came here to watch the sunset and it didn’t disappoint. Make sure you stick to the path otherwise you end up in the jungle very quickly!
title: Great sunset spot

body: It’s such a beautiful hotel. It has a lot of facilities and everything looks absolutely gorgeous!! the breakfast is also amazing. The employees are all so nice and really friendly I want to give a special thank you to sanjeevan, Kapilan, selvi, Anuradhi. We had a really great stay and we Will defenitly visit again.
title: The most gorgeous hotel in all of Sri lanka

body: It is a beautiful hotel, with extremely nice employee's, special thanks to Sanjeevan, the nicest pool boy ever, and Kapilan & Selvi did our rooms realy good, very pretty with all the flowers on the bed. And to Anuradhi, for being an extremely nice waitress. We felt welcome and enyoid our stay a lot. Nice beach and beautiful jungle feeling around the hotel.
title: A beautiful hotel with great service

body: Very average beach more akin to a dumping ground for locals and used as a rubbish dump!Very disappointing how much rubbish is strewn about the trails down to this beach! I would be embarrassed as a local and representative of this area at the state!Once you arrive at this beach it is decidedly average compared to some beautiful spots far easily accessed.
title: Mediocre Beach Amongst Hidden Gems

body: What could be a very nice secluded beach is effectively a beach with fair amount of rubbish every where . These gold really need to establish a proper rubbish disposal and collection
title: Disappointing and underwhelming

body: We walked here and the walk was nice, but I wouldn’t go here for a day trip. Many locals love this beach, which makes it crowded.
title: Waist of time

body: This was a nice morning walk in the jungle to reach the beach. The sea water just tempts you to jump in the ocean as it looks too good. It's a small easy trek which anyone can walk through. Do visit if you are close by
title: Walk to remember

body: A little 20 min walk from Unawatuna brings you to this lovely beach with green calm waters and a very quiet atmosphere. There are two beaches with shade from the trees where you can swim, do snorkeling or only chill. Perfect for families with kids. Close to Jungle Beach is the Japanese Peace Pagoda a very beautiful spot to watch the sunset.
title: Amazing Spot

body: We visited here by motorbike (it would be a good walk from Unawatuna and is bumpy road either way!) in the evening and it was lovely. The beach is small but was full of locals playing football and had a very fun vibe, and the swimming was good. Lovely views of Galle and the coastline, and also a great spot to watch the sunset if you walk up the path from where cars park.It’s near the Japanese Peace Pagoda so worth combining with a visit there.
title: Off the beaten track but worth it

body: You hv to make a short hike to descend to the beach. Not easy for the elderly. Beach itself is small but not too crowded. There are areas which hv nice sand and areas w rocks (so be careful). There are some fish not to far out amongst the rocks if u look for them.
title: Nice Out of the way beach

body: We took a morning walk to Jungle Beach. We wore flip flops, which probably weren’t the most sensible footwear. It’s a bit of a hike downhill, with rocks and bits of shaded jungle. It was a beautiful walk and the beach itself was very pretty. There was a lot of rubbish lying around, but it was lovely to swim in the sea and cool down after getting there. There are two small shops there with cold drinks and beers. Definitely worth a visit.
title: Beautiful beach

body: Beautiful beach but takes damage on the kids and parents if you have to carry them down. Beach could also do with a cleaning as it is filthy..... the views however are fantastic
title: Good but a hustle with young kids

body: Nice beach with tricky access but need to clear rubbish problem.Great sunsets where you can sip a cold drink,”.
title: Tropical beach

body: Jungle beach is about a 20 minute stroll from west Unawatuna. It’s not at all a secret beach! There’s signs most of the way as well as opportunistic fruit and clothes sellers. It’s a well trodden path to a small beach, that has nice shade, two beach bars and a restaurant on the east side. It has views to Galle and snorkelling opportunities. It has a good vibe and local teens like to swim and drum there.
title: Nice stroll to a little beach

body: Small beach located near Unawatuna. Easy to access with bike. Right on the corner near the main road there is bike rental with good prices.
title: Beautiful place

body: Jungle beach ist a must! It is not easy to get there as you have to walk down through the jungle but it is worth it!
title: Beautiful beach

body: It’s quite a little hike through the jungle down a path to a beautiful little local beach where you’ll find as many locals as you will tourists😀You’re a few stand set up to sell food down at the bottom as well as drinks so you don’t necessarily have to pack anything
title: Beautiful local beach

body: Overcrowded on weekends but must go place to visit ! Calm water, soft beach. Love this place! Some places rocky entrance in to the water, but wount make much of a problem. Moderate place for snorkeling. If u travel this part of the world u Must visit this place!
title: Best beach

body: This is a very beautiful beach. However, beach is filled with plastics and garbage. You have to walk around 1Km to reach the beach. There is no restaurant. So you have to carry your own food.
title: Beautiful Beach

body: It was a simple hike to Jungle beach. The beach itself is lovely but very busy with tourists and locals . The trail had lots of garbage , empty beer and booze bottles and cigarettes. Very disappointing!
title: A nice walk ,but trail littered with garbage

body: Calm water, decent snorkelling, monkeys can be seen sometimes. We went by scooter and got charged 100 lkr and were given a dodgy fake receipt. Not the end of the world but just ruins it that locals wanna make unfair money from tourists.
title: Nice getaway from The main beach

body: Came here on morning at around 9.30am and it was really quiet with 2 tourists taking a morning swim and a couple of locals. It's definitely not the easiest beach to walk down to - loose stones in the road towards the beach pathway and then the pathway itself would be quite challenging for some. I can confirm there were around two big piles of trash (water bottles, wrappers etc), which made the beach quite unappealing to swim in. That said, it looks to be an enclosed and small beach, so may be great for families or those looking to escape the tourists.
title: Quite underwhelming!

body: Close to famous Unawatuna beach and Japanese Peace Pagoda, The Jungle Beach is amazing place you need to check out. It's breathtaking view will be prettier with amazing sunset 😍😍
title: Romantic hideaway

body: Nice beach, challenging walk down though, not an easy climb down for those with small children or the elderly or those with mobility issues. Good snorkelling. Very few sun beds available.
title: Nice beach

body: We loved the calm tranquil waters, the beach hut was great with fresh fish and cocktails, just the walk from The top road was hard going in the heat , no good if you have any walking disabilities
title: Paradise but need to be fit for the walk down the rough path

body: Small dark beach would be nice if it would be less tourists. Lost of fish so great for snorkeling but looots of turists
title: Over crowded weekend

body: It is a really good place to sea bath in Galle.Excellent place.Good with the family & friend.It covers with small jungle.No big sunlight also. we enjoyed a lot. Go again soon.
title: Fantastic Beach

body: Took a boat from Unawatuna to come here & snorkel The beach has a lot of people which kicks up the sands quite a lot impairing visibility.Otherwise an okay place , safe since it's a lagoon providing decent snorkelling near the rocky shoreline adjacent to the beach.
title: Snorkeling visit

body: There you can see fish, many fish but during weekend it gets too crowdy. Beter go during weekday for a calm atmosphere
title: Nice place to snorkel!

body: For me it was the most horrible beach I have ever seen in my life! And I saw a lot of beaches in Asia. Waste everywhere. And all tourists are laying next to piles of rubbish as its a normal thing. We were shocked and left immediately. Not worth to go there!
title: More a waste dump than a beach!!!

body: The restaurant food for breakfast and dinner outstanding truly a delight but the accommodation even though the rooms are big was a let down. We stayed in a Jungle room with twin beds that were so rickety and noisy that made sleeping difficult. Also the step down to the bathroom at night was dangerous. The beach was beautiful and pool area reasonably maintained but needed work. On the whole would have been a fabulous experience if rooms and pool been up to scratch.
title: Tired accomodation but food fabulous

body: Early morning was quiet, but became evermore crowded. So much garbage, so sad. Snorkelling was cool, don't do it with a tour/by boat.
title: Dirty beach but beautiful snorkelling

body: Lovely beach. Was bit difficult to get there through the small mountain but it was fun. Better go with good gripping shoes. Once you are in the beach it was lovely. Can do snorkeling too. Many fish near the corals. Highly recommend visiting
title: Beautiful beach

body: We went down on a Sunday when all of the local people head to this beach and it was awesome! Busy but with a wonderful atmosphere of fun. On days other than Sunday it is much much quieter. Road to walk there from Unawatuna bay can be a little tricky but totally worth it.
title: Such a beautiful beach!

body: Small beach near Galle, that despite some fame has nothing special. Not much sand where you can relax, the beach is not secluded and it has some boats even around it. Also it is a beach with a city view in a distance not exactly the palm tree you probably are looking for.It has the reputation of the being one of best near Galle, but nothing special. You will find better places.
title: Small and with a city view

body: Beautiful secluded beach but a little tricky to get tooSteep climb down with stairs only part of the wayBut worth it when u get there
title: Truly amazing

body: A small little downward hike about 10mins or so to this lovely little beach was well worth it.Got here just before midday and was lucky enough to get 2 beach beds.Wasn’t as busy thankfully as I’d expected from reading some of the reviews so had a great time.Food on offer also..Japanese pargoda temple about 15mins up across the rocks to your left and then up a steep incline. We did it in Flip flops no problem.
title: Nice little secluded beach

body: Lovely spot when you get there and relatively small beach so can get crowded. Some shade near the trees to be shared with local dogs. Great for simple free snorkelling with loads of fish. Boats available if you are keener
title: Good but crowded

body: Lovely little beach, bit of a trek to get down to from where the tutu drops you off, well worth a visit
title: Beautiful

body: Its a bit of a hike down and up in the heat but worth for the white sandy beach and azure water. A nice cafe on the beach. "Traditional" toilet...
title: Picuresque beach

body: It sounds ideal, but as you come around the corner and are faced with the sight of hundreds of people and sellers and boats and stalls, the idyllic image quickly shatters. It’s a 20-30 minute hot walk up and down to the beach from the streets of Unawatuna and it’s not worth it once you get there.
title: Crowds

body: Just a short hike through the jungle to get there. Decent beach. A lot more coral/shells on the beach than other beaches in Sri Lanka. Beautiful, but not fun to walk on. Sad to see garbage all over the beach. Recommend heading there early to get a spot in the shade.
title: Nice beach, short hike

body: I saw no hips of trash described; the beach itself is rocky and small, but you may enjoy its peaceful waters. Many locals swimming.
title: Nice Hidden Beach

body: Jungle beach is very beautiful, but it's a shame visitors and locals throw trash everywhere. There is no proper trash can and it seems that nobody cares about environmental destruction.
title: Too much litter

body: We coupled a visit to Jungle Beach with an early morning start at the close by Japanese Peace Pagoda. We arrived at Jungle Beach at around 8:00am and had the beach to ourselves. Beautiful sands and waters. I can however imagine this place gets very busy after around 9:00am, we left when others started to arrive.
title: Visit Early and Beat the Crowds

body: If you want a beach to your self here you go, wake up early and either trek or catch a ride to the Jungle beach, if you reach here by 7-8am the place is your, enjoy a morning dip, with no one in sight. Romantic, peaceful and relaxing. Must Visit!
title: Hidden Jem

body: If you want to swim the waves might be an issue here but if you don’t mind large waves when you go for a dip. Jungle beach is for you. There is a small bar where you can have a beer I would not go for any food there.
title: Average beach

body: We loved it here. The beach is great for swimming as it’s very sheltered.There was no rubbish as suggested by previous posts, in fact a few chaps from the Sri Lankan Navy turned up in a boat to litter pick whilst we were there. There were a lot of local family enjoying the beach which was very nice to see.We preferred it to Unawatuna beach which reminded me of Bournemouth, but with more bars!
title: Lovely beach

body: This is a very pretty little beach off the beaten track. It is quite popular though, not so secret nowadays. They have a juice bar doing juices, milkshakes and cocktails. Walk to the beach is through the jungle - lovely. Nice place for a swim and relax.
title: Nice beach

body: lovely beach .. can have fun with sea bathing and the beautiful views. can enjoy with the family and friends
title: nice beach

body: Worst beach we’ve been too in Sri Lanka, plastic and rubbish floating around... rubbish on beach... not nice. We left after 10 minutes. Very disappointed, nothing like the photos
title: Swim

body: Get there early as it’s small and starts to get busy later. Gorgeous beach to enjoy a coconut on. Steep hill to get there though. Right near the Japanese peace pagoda so you can combine the trip if it’s a tuktuk ride away for you
title: Beautiful beach

body: Great little beach about 30 minute walk from Unawatuna. Did the walk in Jandals/slippers/thongs. Go very early in the morning as the crowds start coming in from 9am onwards.
title: Great secluded beach - go early morning

body: Relaxing, clean and peaceful. Bit of a trek to reach but worth the rock crossing. The second beach is the better of the two.
title: Lovley

body: The rubbish underfoot tarnished any natural beauty except from a landscape perspective. If you are looking for a happening party beach at the expense of nature, Jungle beach is for you. I left after a few minutes, as the volume of litter ruined my mood.
title: Hiking Through Trash

body: not worth it folks bit disappointed better elsewherelong walk down to beach and not much room to put towel down
title: poor beach

body: Was really nice but super busy being a public holiday.Trek down is a challenge with little kids and older parents
title: Morning swim

body: I'm glad we went, as the monkeys in the tree were cute. The middle of the beach had rocks, so it was best to swim either end of the bay. It was a trek down the hill to get there and there is only one restaurant and all the sunbeds were taken so we laid on the sand. I liked it for a change, however we only visited the once.
title: Glad I visited...

body: This is a delightful beach in its own little cove. It is nicely sheltered and offers reasonably good snorkelling very close-by the shore. The fact that you have to walk a bit to get here is a big plus.We came two days before Independence day, which was a Saturday, so it was probably one of the busiest days, which meant it was overcrowded. There was also a disappointing amount of litter.I feel that if you came mid-week and it was not a major national holiday, this place would be really special.
title: A lovely beach - best mid-week

body: It was worth the walk to get there - much more pleasant than the local beach which tended to be a bit dirty at low tide
title: Less populated beach

body: Very nice jingle beach near by galle habour and also ancient fort of south c9ast of sri lanka.y9u can enjoy there very very freedom with sun,sand and sea.
title: Sun and sea

body: Nice place, but way to beach is very difficult. No way to get there with some health problems. Water is ok for smsll kids, and adults can swim there too. Food there is tasty, and you have choices. The water was clean.
title: Nice

body: Full of people & worst of all...plastic garbage! Visitors please take your trash with you and please stop using a new plastic straw for every coconut you buy.
title: Not so secret

body: Great place for swimming since there aren’t waves that would make it dangerous. We went there on Sunday and there were many locals playing ball and singing.
title: Great place for swimming

body: a different beach . Many close by major attractions including Galle fort and Rumassala peace pagoda.
title: a different beach

body: While the boom in tourism is great for Sri Lanka it means previously secluded or quiet places like Jungle Beach are no longer off the beaten path or a secret. When we visited there were at least 100 people in the first small beach. Also filthy with rubbish.
title: No longer secluded

body: Lovely beach accessible by a bit of a climb down a rocky path. Little shack on the beach who have sunbeds if you buy food/drink from them. Sadly lots of litter on and around the beach and in the water. Not idyllic crystal clear water for sure which is a shame. On our visit, lots of noisy Russians who decided it was ok to play their crap Euro pop at full volume from a portable speaker. Oddly the men spend a lot of time taking photos of their wives/girlfriends in various soft porn style poses. Maybe we where unlucky but as in Thailand it is better if you can find the places the Russians haven't.
title: Spoilt by litter & Russians

body: Like an undiscovered Beach! I went there to see sunset and fullmoon. So romantic and beautiful!!!!!!
title: Beautiful by Night!

body: It is sad, such a awesome place. Swimming with turtles, but sharing the experience with loads of plastic. Don't be a muppet, clean your filth.
title: Take your trash!

body: Beautiful place to visit. Walking through the jungle next to the temple walk down to the beach only sad thing about this place it was not clean too many disposed plastic :( best for nature lovers and to do snorkelling on the way you will see monkeys 😍🐵🐒🐠🦀
title: Beautiful but crowded

body: The walk to this beach was full of rubbish. Distressing. The place is filthy and full of people drinking and with loud music. There is NO snorkling to be done. On leaving we decided to tale a tuk tuk and they are slmost mafia like. We eventually called a pick me car for a third of the price and the tuk tuk drivers ganged up on the driver when he arrived, stole his keys from the ignition and used a police like batton to hit him.Dont bother going here
title: Dont waste your time here

body: Enjoyed a snorkel off the rocks and spent quite a lot of time watching sizeable puffer fish in action! Took my wife and daughter and felt safe as not a fast current...
title: Great spot for snorkelling

body: one of the most beautiful beaches I've seen in my lifebest way to get here is a scutertake diving/snorkling masks with you because there is a good spot for diving/snorkling
title: one of the most beautiful beaches

body: Little bit to much tourists. Wouldn't go there anymore. Tiny beach. A lot of people and to many boats.
title: Not what you expect

body: What to write about this “beautiful” place. Full of garbage and people. It is truly a jungle beach, but i do not have the urge to pay a second visit to this place. There are much nicer beaches in south coast of SL
title: Upps

body: As much as I thought it was a beautiful spot, tourists (and possibly locals) have let it down by leaving litter behind on the beach. I feel the lack of bins hasn’t helped this, but it’s still everyone’s responsibility to clean up after themselves.
title: Litter let it down!

body: Please note there are 2 jungle beaches next to each other, but the entrances are 500 m apart. The one marked on Google maps and towards the end of the road is just Jungle Beach, and the one before that is White Jungle Beach. The latter is more beautiful. There is good swimming and sunbathing on both. The white beach has a beachside bar and restaurant, while the other one also has vendors selling beer, coconuts etc.The beaches are also good for snorkelling. The left end of the white beach has good reefs with fish. The other beach has reefs on both ends with similar fish. You might get snorkels for rent from one of the vendors on the beach but recommend renting from one of the dive centers in Unawatuna.
title: Beautiful and peaceful beach

body: You can walk there or take a TukTuk.A lot of local people are using this beach, and that says it all.
title: No people, great beach and beautiful natur.

body: Full of rocks inside the see, there is garbage everywhere... I didn't like it at all and wouldn't recommend it.
title: Bad idea to go

body: Think this beach is more for young fit people as it was a quite a trek to get there.it is aptly named as you had to go through a mini jungle to get to it.
title: Quite a trek

body: A short ride by tuc tuc and you reach this little gorgeous beach. Calm, a restaurant snd some sun chakra.
title: Best beach near Unawatuna

body: Flat beach with calm waves..found it peaceful n could easily spend couple of hrs swimming n snorkeling in the clear water.The walking route to beach via jungle is great experience as well. Its a short walk though.
title: Good beach for swimming and snorkling

body: We went during the public holidays so it was so busy with lots of noise, people & trash everywhere. There was so many public buses that was taking everyone there knocking anyone & any other vehicle off the roads.The poor monkeys was eating plastic bags full of peoples trash that they all carelessly chuck aside. Disgusting seeing what could of been a beautiful spot completely ruined.
title: Overcrowed, dirty, smelly & full of trash!

body: An idyllic and quiet spot about 20 minutes from Galle Fort. 500 Rupees in a Tuk Tuk. Then a 200mtr walk through lush rain forest down to a secluded beach. Get there early to secure a wooden Deck Chair,say 9:30am. Beach bar serves cocktails, spirits and beer and some meals.
title: Idyllic and Quiet

body: 25 min by walk from Unawatuna and down the road you can meet monkeys and vaarans. The beach is 'movie-style'. No sunbeds but you can easily hide from the sun under the trees. Warm and quiet sea that is good for kids and for swimming. You can snorkle and see some fishes next to the stones of your right hands. And i strongly recommend to try mojito and pina colada with only people who serve it by the ground boat. The best in Una!
title: Cool and lovely

body: The beach is very small and while visiting we noticed a big commotion in one of the small areas. It was monkeys eating all the trash gathered on the side of the beach! There are a few small carts selling coconuts, water and juice but then there is no place to throw the trash out so it’s gathered on the side. Dalawella beach was much better, even the main Unawatuna beach is cleaner and in my opinion, nicer to stay at.
title: Crowded and dirty

body: We made the mistake of getting here close to sunset. There's a 10 minute walk to through the trees to get to the beach. It's not at all lit up so make sure you have a torch of some kind on you. It can be a bit slippery and there are a lot of mosquitoes so take your repellent! The beach was nice, buzzing with locals, music, families and we enjoyed ourselves.
title: Fun beach!

body: You can take a tuk tuk but we walked. It was super crowded and not very big. Not worth the trek at all. There are quite a few monkeys though.
title: Not great

body: For us, the place was a bit crowded. We went on a Saturday and beside tourists, a lot of local people came. But it is amazing there. You have to walk down a jungle until you reach the beach. Water was very clear, sand very clean... paradise indeed
title: Amazing

body: Cannot say that I am amazed by this beach, as it is quite small and crowded. It must have been a lonely place some time ago, but surely not now.
title: Crowded and quite small

body: I should have listened to what I read. I should. That is the reason for this site. Despite, I read the reviews and I plodded on, misguidedly shunning the information I had read. Scootering up the hill from the Galle Road, caught up in a fracas between the private blue coaches, belching diesel fumes, and ferocious tuk tuk drivers who seem to think they are in the cast of wacky races and far more aggressive, thankfully with each other as opposed to the fat westerner on his borrowed moped. Reaching the top, we park, we walk, down down down the litter strewn Hill, over cobbles and past other weary travelers and locals making their way back up. We arrive, and what a load of rubbish. Literally, a load of rubbish. The beach itself, I imagine could be quite nice, but yet again the human race has let itself down, and ruined a place that could be so beautiful. If you go, expect to feel sad. I did.
title: Should have listened. Proceed with caution.

body: The beach is very unclean and trashy. There are lots of plastic in the sea and also in the beach and the jungle. I ordered bottle of coke from jungle beach bar and it was warm not cool. The beach could be nice if trash and plastic cleaned out of the beach.
title: Trashy Beach

body: The beach was too crowdy with the local people,quite a lot of stones and corals in the water so you easily get hurt your toe. Only one restaurant - the prices quite high.
title: Too crowdy

body: A disappointing visit in which we picked our way through rubbish to reach the beach. The sea was full of plastic bags.
title: Litter and rocks

body: This "genuine jungle beach" resembled a dumping ground. A jungle road led here from Unawatuna and we were horrified how much plastic and other junk was dumped all over the sides of the path. The beach itself looked okay for swimmers but we left almost instantly upon arriving because of the bad treatment of nature. Authorities should pay this place more attention and the people visiting here should definitely take care of their junk. I felt so sad for this place and still am.
title: Please take care of the nature, this place is full of plastic

body: Good sandy beach protected by the bay. The local municipality needs to provide some bins to collect the plastic.There is a risk that this amazing beach could become another rubbish dump
title: Beach time

body: We walked here from our accommodation in Unawatuna beach, there were helpful direction signs to assist us finding the beach. As it was a Saturday the beach was busy but not too crowded. Nice for a swim and no currents in the water
title: Busy but good for a visit

body: We visited this beach based on the iddylic descriptions, but we were disappointed. Sadly, the beach is beautiful but human interference has ruined it. The path down to the beach is well maintained and even swept but the rubbish is just swept off the path into the trees. Having secured a shady spot under a beautiful tree, we were often greeted with wafts of the odour of rotting rubbish which was piled up just behind us. Beach visitors should be encouraged to clean up their litter and the businesses should also take better measures to clean up. If you want to swim, just be cautious as you enter the sea. There is a lot of sharp and broken coral and rocks so kids are likely to get a scrape or two! In such a pretty setting, we were happy to deal with this as it's nature, but disappointed by the litter - my son fished out 3 plastic bags from the shore.
title: Not worth the hype

body: Visited on a Sunday afternoon and never have I seen so much fresh litter across one beach! The beach was packed with locals enjoying the sun, but seemingly unable to clean up after themselves. It’s a 10 minute hike down the beach and not at all worth it.
title: Just Not Good

body: The beach was lovely with lots of locals on the weekend who were nice and chatty. After seeing reviews saying the beach was dirty we were concerned but only saw one tiny bit of litter.I’d recommend getting dropped off near the beach and walking down as it’s only 5 minutes compared to the hike from Unawatuna. Be warned though as it is quite steep in places.I’d recommend going a bit earlier in the day as it started to get busy at about 2pm.Reasonably priced food and drink on the beach as well.
title: Lovely little beach

body: Its a long and arduous hike from Unawatuna, and when you get there, it's small, a bit crowded, with one stall selling drinks. It's also not very clean, with plastic bottles and rubbish all over the place
title: Not worth it

body: Amazing beach.way better than Unawatuna.great guys working at the bar on the beach.you can have drinks and dinner there.well worth it.tuk tuk from Una around 400 ruppies (don't pay more)
title: great beach

body: The ocean itself is nice but the surroundings let it down massively. There is rubbish everywhere and the place is kind of trashy. The crowd is largely international. If you are looking for nice ambience and a nice place to swin, better to go to Unawatuna. This is one of those examples where unorganised tourism lets the traveller and the environment down. It would not take much for the Government and locals to clean up and take care of the place, and the actual access to the place. I wouldnt recommend going here.
title: A once upon a time gem...now full of trash

body: We need trek down to reach this beach. Quite secluded. Eye catching water color. They even have tier swing.The view is really good. The beach restaurant people annoy you at times. The beach is not that clean.
title: Nice view but no clean water.

body: Upon reaching the parking area, visitors would need to hike down for about 10-20minutes, depending on your age and fitness level. Word of caution to families travelling with young children and the elderly, as there are some rather steep drops and slippery corners to get to the beach. Hence it is recommended to wear good shoes. The beach was a beautiful blue👍 Glimpses of tiny, transluscent fishes swimming all about the water. Plenty of shade around to set up a picnic basket. Once done dipping, shower areas and changing rooms are available at a reasonable price back at the parking area. We truly enjoyed this experience with 2 elderly ladies and 3 young children in tow and highly recommend it!
title: Beautiful sunny afternoon

body: It’s a cool little place and I tucked away down a small path. There’s also a bar so you will not be thirsty here :) it’s a small beach with nice water.Very chilled vibe
title: Cozy gem

body: Nice place to relax, good drinks, nice view (3/5)It’s a hike down from the main road where also you can find monkeys 🐒.
title: Nice place to relax

body: I had only heard great things about jungle beach so decided it was definitely worth a visit.I walked there from Unawatuna and was glad I'd read reviews on here describing how to get there because it is not really signposted until you are almost there. I enjoyed the walk and locals were helpful in pointing me in the right direction. Don't expect an easy stroll - it is quite a trek on uneven and narrow trails with large rocks. However, you may be lucky to see monitor lizards, peacocks and other animals along the way like I did. When I got to the beach I was quite disappointed - maybe it was the time of year but the water was rough and dirty, the sands were littered with rubbish and debris. My belief that I could snorkel in tranquil waters and see lots of beautiful fish was instantly killed. In the 5 mins I tried to go into the water, I got scratched quite badly by rocks you cannot see through the murky waters. Even when I tried to go into the water further up the beach, I quickly got out again due to the amount of rubbish wrapping itself around my legs. Such a shame - but I bet the waters are calmer, clearer and the beach cleaner at high season in Summer.At least I saw a huge monitor lizard - that was really cool.
title: Jungle beach - Disappointing

body: Jungle Beach is really a short walk from Unawatuna (about 40-60 min) through the jungle then climb down to the beach that is secluded and overlooks Galle.First came here over 3 years ago and it felt more exciting back then as it really was like a trek in the jungle but this time, felt that Unawatuna in general and the walk to Jungle Beach was now becoming more built up and busy. The walk passes through dozens and dozens of hotels and B&B's and it is likely to be more crowded and busy once the monstrosity of a hotel is built in the Unawatuna beach! So better get here quick before it loses its charm.The positives is that because the area still belongs to the Dept of Wildlife, they have stopped or done away with the previous make-shift restaurants that were right by the beach at Jungle Beach.It seems to be more of a place where a lot of locals come in for a day/weekend trip. Since we went there on a Sunday, it was very busy. Also a tad noisy but everyone seemed to be having a good time. You can swim here too but the sea is now seems to be littered.Strangely though the walk from Unawatuna and though the jungle seemed clean and came across only a few discarded PET bottles.The climb is only slightly difficult but recommend shoes unless you are a flip-flop pro in which case you can still easily do the climb up and down unless you are unlucky to do the trek on a rainy day.Make sure to take lots of water though, as it is humid.There are a few restaurants around in the vicinity before you climb down to the beach that offers local food for good prices. We didn't have lunch there, so no idea how the food was.If you don't fancy eating after the walk, you can always a grab a bite to eat once you get to Dalewala road which has all the touristy shops/restaurants.
title: Fancy a short trek that leads you to the beach? Recommend the Jungle Beach Trek

body: Visited this beach via a tuk tuk for a morning with my family (3 adults, 4 children ages 7, 6, 3, & 1.) First off, there are two beaches to jungle beach and we visited the beach which is closer to the temple, I think it is the smaller beach and is known for snorkeling. As to the snorkeling, don't waste your time. Very little fish to see, no coral, and poor water clarity (and I think we were on a good day for water clarity.) Honestly, we brought our snorkel gear on our trip to Sri Lanka because of hopes to snorkel at jungle beach, if I go back, I won't bother carrying the stuff with me. The beach itself was nice in the morning with a good amount of tourists, but not enough to be crowded. Around about noon things started to get busy as many mothers were coming to the beach with their kids after school let out. I didn't find any issue with this group of people other than the fact that there were a ton of them. They just kept coming and coming and things were getting really crowded. I am talking about going from roughly 50 - 60 tourists at the beach to probably 200+ after school crowd and growing. So we decided to pack up and move on.If you want a somewhat secluded, calm beach with kind of clear water, then come by Jungle Beach in the morning and enjoy. Other than that, I wouldn't bother coming to this beach. Honestly, when back in Sri Lanka, I won't visit this beach again. There are way better places than this.
