We ended up swimming in the rain, its a lovely bay even in the rain can only imagine what it's like in the sun. Worth a visit.
title: Enjoyable visit

body: An ok place. Nice beach, warm wAter and a down hill walk- not for everyone.Food and drinks available.
title: Nice beach

body: We booked a snorkelling trip with the Taxi Service Office for two people $50:00,We were picked up at 08:30 as planned and taken by tuk tuk to unawatuna beach and then by two local guys to jungle beach,On arrival by boat we were offered to snorkel by jungle beach but the water is not clear and certainly not snorkelling water, many rocks also which are dangerous where my partner cut her toe,Would not recommend unawatuna for snorkelling,,,,,
title: Snorkelling

body: Definitely worth a visit if in Unawatuna, as the beach is lovely and relatively secluded, without tons of restaurants like Unawatuna main beach. There is a small beach bar with drinks and some food choices and sun loungers.Getting there - follow signs from Unawantuna foot paths. You will be walking on a trail through the jungle until you get to a first beach (this is not Jungle Beach). From here, go to the end of this first beach and find the trail entry point to walk another 10 minutes to Jungle Beach. Total hike time is approximately 30-45 minutes. You will be walking on rocky trails - doable in flip flops if you're used to it; wear sneakers if you're not comfortable walking on uneven terrains. Recommended to go either in the morning or late afternoon to avoid mid-day heat.
title: Beautiful, quiet beach, after hiking through the Jungle from Unawatuna

body: I absolutely loved it here! There is a short, tricky, (in flip flops) walk down, through jungle, from the road, to the beach. This was fun though because the trees were filled with monkeys. The beach was relatively quiet, which I also liked. The sea was very calm here, unlike other places such as Bentota and Negumbo where it was rough. The reason I loved it so much was that the snorkelling was amazing!! It was like swimming in a huge aquarium. There were fishes of all colours and sizes, many I hadn't seen before and the absolute bonus was there were also turtles. This would have been a completely perfect experience, but there was quite a bit of rubbish around the edges of the beach, I think, probably washed up by the tide. I would still fully recommend a visit or even two or three to this beach, especially if you enjoy snorkelling, it was the best beach I experience in the whole holiday. Drinks, beer etc. are available to buy.
title: A wonderful beach

body: A good place to visit. I recommend this place to any one. In Galle you can buy fish from fresh market but keep in mind they use 2 prize tag one is for locals and one in for foreigners. So before buy or use any thing ask few local about the actual pricing.
title: Family Trip

body: The way to this beach is not easy but it is worth it. We went there on Sunday and met mostly local people. The beach has spectacular views
title: Very nice beach for locals

body: A day in beach with delight, fun and observing with the nature of it's own make your self convienient to make a full of it by snorkeling, yachting, surfing and enlight the excitement.Cool & calm beach, made the delight of staying top of the rocks hanging around watching the excitement. Don't forget to bring your beach out fits, (Snorkeling, Slippers Etc...) water, snacks along the way and it's a fullfilling amaze for the family to hang around.Excellent place to be... Amazing!!!It's nature been bit out of order maybe it should develop the habitats of the coral reefs, be in a watchful eye for your belongings, be aware to take a little hike by walking.Please preserve the nature...!!! Dump the trash at the trash containers if not don't ever leave it behind... Make a moment for future generations too... Keep it tidy...!!!:::[Best Beach Experience]:::
title: Sizzling Beach...!!!

body: We walked to jungle beach from Unawatuna beach took about 20-25 minutes. There are a few stops along the way that sell snacks and cold water. Jungle beach itself seemed to have more locals than tourists, which was nice. Plenty of shade, lovely beach.
title: Hidden away!

body: Great beach with great views and few people but with reefs and rocks. Good place to snorkling but difficult to swim and enjoy the waters without get injured.
title: Nice but not for swimming

body: The walk to Jungle Beach is great! One can see monkeys, the Japanese Pagoda, stop by the side of the road and drink some coconut water, etc. The views are simply spectacular. Once at the beach, then things get a bit disappointing: trash everywhere, from condom wrappers to discarded water bottles and everything in between. This is a preferred spot for locals who come in large groups to party at the beach. The beach itself is nice enough but the view is dreadful: looking out from the beach into the horizon, one sees the entire port and industrial Galle complex in the near distance. The opposite of the idyllic images “jungle beach” conjures. I stayed about half an hour and walked back to Unawatuna beach with its wonderful never ending horizon to look at, not an industrial/port facility. There is a restaurant before one goes down to the beach which is nice and worth visiting. If you are looking for a walk, this is the place to go, if you are looking for a pristine, off the beaten path beach, THIS IS NOT that place.My advise is to stay in Unawatuna and beyond, the beaches are easily accessed and the views and spaces more relaxing and beautiful. Not sure why Jungle Beach has been built up so much in the tourist “must see” activities.
title: A nice walk but the beach is not so nice

body: We walked to this beach several times starting in unatwatuna, and the walk was really nice. the beach itself is also nice and in a idyllic setting, but there is also quite some waste laying around and sometimes people come with boats, so that it might not be that quiet sometimes.Water was nice, didn't see so many fish though. For us the tour walking there, having a a swim, relax a bit and walking back as a whole was the real adventure. Recommend the trip!(there is just one restaurant and a few stops with coconuts and water on the way, the beach itself does not have anything to eat or drink, which suits the peacefullness of the place. just keep that in mind when packing your bag!)
title: Walk there from unawatuna, the trip itself is really nice!

body: This is a gorgeous beach in a beautiful setting. It is perfect for young kids as the sea is tranquil. It is also quite romantic with various shady places for young couples to be alone. I imagine the snorkeling is good too give the tranquillity and slow incline of the coast. I would rate this a five but for the fact that it was a bit dirty in the sea (I removed a bottle wrapper and a dirty cloth whilst my wife removed a bit of glass and placed in the bins). We both also managed to cut ourselves on the rocks in the sea but this was due to not taking care in the water. This isn't a place for folks with mobility issues unless they are coming by boat as the climb down from the road is a bit steep and rocky.
title: Nice beach - little bit dirty and quite crowded

body: We saw the sign 'jungle beach' and thought it was worth exploring. It is a bit of a hike, up and down two hills, to get there, and that is the real interesting part as you pass trough a jungle-type of area. Once there, the first part of the beach is a bit congested (again with local boats) but the larger part, for which you have a pass a rocky area towards Galle/West, is more quiet. Great for swimming (rocky coast, clear water)
title: Hidden treasure yet quite crowded - walking there is the real attraction

body: We were advised this beach a few times by our tuk-tuk driver. Remote and isolated indeed. Yet, the beach is located in the closed bay of Galle and is therefore unfortunately dirty... beach itself and most importantly water.So many other beaches are so great around... avoid this one.
title: Dirty water

body: Jungle beach is a great place to chill. Visited with friends in December. Trip to Mirissa was on Xmas day. Got to Jungle beach at around 9.30am and had the beach to ourself. It started getting crowded around 11am. Getting to location is a bit tough but that’s what is great about the place.
title: Great isolated beach

body: To isolated and if you have any walking problems can be difficult to reach unless you take boat trip.
title: Beach

body: We got the feeling that jungle beach would be a little paradise. Pretty disappointed I was. Small, dirty and indifferent. But the walk to it was nice
title: Exciting walk but pointless beach

body: One of the most beautiful beaches in Sri Lanka :) almost a Maldives touch :))) very recommended once you’re in Unawatuna.
title: Cannot be missed

body: The beach itself is small, and nice enough, accessed by a very dicey path down through the greenery from the road but unfortunately tourists are animals and have made a real mess of it. Piles of garbage at the tree line make it very sad indeed, and no effort seems to be made to clean it up. Not sure it was really worth a trip.
title: Nice but needs the trash picking up

body: It was so good that more than unawatuna beach we had more privacy here,not much crowded, its best for teenagers and couples
title: Wish i could buy this land

body: One of the greatest and marvelous beach in the Sri Lanka wich situated in down-south,Sri Lanka. Very peaceful and attractive beach. There’s a very famous story stick with the Rumassala mountain next to the beach about Rama and king Rawana. This beach may have very peaceful and beautiful nature and please visitors have keep it up and clean the environment.
title: Marvelous beach

body: It is one of the best views in Sri Lanka in Unawatuna. Jungale beach is super blue view and blue water can be enjoyed by anyone. it is very green jungle the road to the beach which should be walk along.
title: The natural view

body: The walk was great, the beach itself is not worth staying. Dont expect a hidden blue lagoon. There is a cocktailbar and quite a bit of people, locals and tourists. The place is polluted and lost quite a bit of its charm it must have had 10 years ago.
title: The walk to it was good...

body: The beach is well looked after by the people that work there. They clean up any litter in the morning. It’s sad that there is litter that has to be cleaned up in the first place. Otherwise it’s a really beautiful beach and the sea is pretty calm. You can walk there from Unawatuna. A nice morning or afternoon excursion. I would recommend going early in the morning to avoid the busy times and on the weekends there is sometimes loud music which was a huge put off.
title: A nice change of scenery

body: Great short walk from Unawatuna, save yourself for a 50rp coconut on the way back. Nice to be walking through a bushy area. The beach was very crowded by 10am, glad we chose to go early and everyone is jostling for shade. Worth snorkelling, saw some lovely fish. The rubbish is overwhelming, as it is in a lot of Sri Lanka, please make sure you dont add to it and carry your rubbish including your cigarette butts out!
title: Crowded by 10am

body: The calmest sea we visited, clean water we could see different types of fish swimming around us, its a very small beach and gets crowded at the weekend. their is a restaurant a short walk away. to walk from Unawatuna is a little hard with steep hills both up and down and very uneven rocky paths we loved it
title: Best swim in Sri Lanka

body: Beach was nice but super busy. Doesn't seem worth traveling to this beach when busier than main unawatuna beach. View of peace pagoda and jungle area from beach is nice.
title: Would skip

body: It's a shame about this beach as it ticks a lot of boxes. It's in an idyllic location cut off and surrounded by jungle, soft sand and lovely calm waters to swim in. Unfortunately it's way too busy, with rubbish everywhere and dirty water. This is due to it's popularity when we arrived it was so busy that we left after half an hour and went to Unawatuna.
title: Small dirty beach

body: Small beach close to Unawatuna. Took a tuk-tuk from hotel. Paid 500 each way and was dropped of right by the path down to the beach. Came around 9am and had beach almost to ourself. Do get busier, but did not feel crowded and one can snorkle.
title: Come see for yourself

body: This beach is supposed to be really special. The walk there is interesting though hard through the ‘jungle’. The beach however is nothing special.
title: Totally overrated

body: We had a great afternoon at jungle BEACH, The water is very clear and you can do some snorkling alone the shore.
title: Nice BEACH!

body: This beach should be wonderful but has a litter problem at the end.You need to go south or east away from the crowds
title: Should be beautiful but has litter at the end

body: Ok beach, but so much overrated. It’s isolated yes - but that's about it. Filled with rubbish laying between the trees. I went snorkeling, but disappointed because a thin layer of sand covered rocks and corals and hardly no fish to seeChoose Dalawella Beach instead.But You can see the pagoda in the same time..
title: Overrated beach

body: I read about this beach good reviews , but we were dissapointed. Watter were so dirty and muddy .we stayed there only one hour and go to another place
title: Dirty place

body: I had read lots of reviews saying that this beach was dirty and covered in litter but I found it perfectly clean! The walk down to the beach isn't difficult. It has a clear path and steps most of the way. There are no big waves so the water is perfect for swimming in. There are a few stalls on the road before walking down to the beach selling drinks and snacks. Here you will also find tuk tuks waiting for when you want to go home. On the beach itself there is a bar selling drinks and snacks. The scenery here is beautiful. You can walk from here up to the beautiful Japanese Peace Pagoda which I recommend going to for sunset.
title: Beautiful little beach, great for swimming

body: My husband and I visited Jungle beach and had the best day. Little cozy beach where you can get fresh juice and milkshakes from the bar at the beach. Lots of locals and a good place for snorkeling as well.
title: Cozy little beach

body: Nice beach, mainly used by locals. no real facilities except for one very basic beach cafe & no sunbeds
title: Steep Rocky Climb Down

body: This is a wonderful beach with moderate tide strength. Nice sand and clear water, also this place is good for calm peace lovers. There are two beach shacks, where you can eat food. Occasionally you can see some wedding photo shoot happening in this beach.The saddest fact I noticed is ocean&Beach pollution is tremendously hight in this beach... I have tried my best to pick up the trash.. Still people should think before they throw plastics in the sea. The beauty of the beach was spoiled due to plenty of trash.If you plan to go.. I would strongly recommend to contribute your share in cleaning this beach.
title: This beach is really good for shallow swimming.

body: We went to Jungle beach and we’re pleasantly surprised.You have a long walk down through thin jungle to reach the beach but when you get there it is full of tourists relaxing with cocktails from a pop up bar that is there.There Still was pollution in the sea but less than other places in Sri Lankan.First and only time we got in the water in a 3 week period.Worth the visit
title: Lovely clean beach with white sands

body: Nice walk through jungle to this small, simple beach with plenty of shadow.No chairs, no food, only some coconuts and softdrinks for sale.When we were there (2 days), there were also groups of Sri Lankan men, dancing, singing and drumming together. For some people a noise, for us a joy
title: Nice walk through jungle to this small, simple beach with plenty of shadow.

body: We were staying in a hotel near Unawatuna beach and it was just over a 30 minute walk to Jungle beach. We walked along a track for 15 minutes before it became much more rugged and we had to climb up and down a rocky path. Before going down to the beach we visited the Peace Pagoda but remember to take your own refreshments as there is no cafe at the beach. The Jungle beach is in a small cove but because it was a Sunday when we were visited, it was very busy and we wished we had visited on a weekday. It is a nice beach to enjoy a swim as it is very protected and at the top of the cliff there was a nice cafe to enjoy a drink.
title: A busy weekend visit

body: It is a nice beach ( small One ) located among the jungle ,it is quite beach with no deep water like other beaches
title: Nice small beach

body: As it says the jungle meets the beach, the walk down is quite short and a Tuk tuk can take you most of the way. It involves a few rocks but manageable in flip flops and not only for the bravehearted and worth the views at the end. Facilities at the beach are limited but cold drinks/water/fresh fruit and snorkel masks available. The beach is smaller compared to nearby unwatuna but not as many people make the journey and trees provide good shade for those taking rest for the sun. Sea is generally calm and plenty of fish to see. Definitely worth a trip.
title: Absolutely stunning

body: Nice nature. It is real similar to a jungle landscape. Also the monkeys are funny. The sand is very yellow and fine. But never in my not so short life I have seen so much rubbish on the beach!
title: disturbed nature

body: This beach is good for a visit but not to stay longer. It doesnt have enough space also crowded on the day i went. most of them were locals.
title: Small beach with bit of local crowd

body: Nice Beach , you have to walk down to the jungle first. But beware of the many rocks in the water. That was My mistake!
title: Nice

body: If you don’t mind flocks of Russian tourists, this is a great place to go to for a swim.Of course this could just be a matter of councidence.
title: Cute little beach

body: It's a very small beach in the jungles. Not the best place for family, but must be visit with friends. Take about 10 minutes walking from pagoda
title: Small nice beach with crabs

body: If you plan your trip to Galle, you must visit this beach. It is 1.5Km journey from Galle-Matara -Hambanthota- Wellayawa road, Rumassala junction (Jungle Beach Junction). Junction is just after passing the bridge near INSEE cement plant Galle. This road will lead to a top of the jungle beach where you have to step down through a dark jungle to reach this hidden beach.Best place to watch Sunset in Galle. A place where mountain steep and beach meets.
title: Jungle Beach

body: We should have taken notice of some previous reviews! This is a grotty little beach, backed by lots of rubbish. You have to walk down a rocky path to get to it, there are other, nicer places to go.
title: Save your energy!

body: Although secluded, this beach was the busiest of all in Unawatuna. Probably since it is so small. There are better options.
title: Busy, not worth the trip

body: i ve really looked forward to go to the jungle beach once in Sri Lanka ,but i found it too small,and poluted! garbage everywhere ! even if it was isolated we spent couple of minutes there and than left. one positive thing is the jungle path leading to it,we encountered monkeys and beautiful flora!
title: Was Expecting more!

body: I love this beach because it is so small, hidden behind the trees and rocks and never crowded!There are a few cabanas that sell drinks and some food (not good food, stick to the basics). The beach has a few long chairs for you to relax and sun bathe.A 5 minute hike is required to see or even get to the beach... definitely worth it :)
title: Small, gorgeous and not crowded

body: We took a tuk tuk to this beautiful sounding beach and on arrival we weren’t disappointed. Gorgeous sandy beach, a little cove and sea was clear and inviting. We walked a little along the beach, past the sun beds and bar/restaurant. Took some lovely photos and then we arrived at the dump site! Loads of bottles, packets, plastic stuff - it was really sad to see as only down the road is a turtle sanctuary! David Attenborough would not approve of the site we saw, too upsetting to actually take a picture. I would recommend you visit as it is a gorgeous little cove, you just have to put the rubbish out of your mind. Please Sri Lanka love your beautiful country and clean it up!
title: Not what I expected!

body: We went for A walk from Unawatuna beach to Jungle Beach. The Nice Little beach had A Little snack bar. The water was extremely clear. I recommend this beach. On your way You can buy Coconut water and pinapples along the Road😃👍🏼🇱🇰
title: Beautiful beach - Nice walk

body: I really enjoyed the walk up the hills and through the village and jungle to the beach. The beach was a little crowded but the water was beautiful. Head to the Japanese Peace Pagoda too as it's at the top of the hill.
title: Fun walk with a beautiful beach at the end

body: Great beach for kids and very beautiful ! Only road is among jungle . But if u like the nature u will like it
title: Nice beautiful beach

body: These are very close together and can be done on the same Tuk Tuk journey from Unawatuna. The driver stayed with us at the JPP then dropped us off at Jungle Beach for 3 hours before returning.Relatively small beach down a steep path with just one vendor, backed by dense trees. Not as good as the main Unawatuna beach.
title: Jungle Beach via Japanese Peace Pagoda

body: We went to Jungle beach by boat. Beach is small. In that day were crowded. For snorkelling is fine, but not much of corals, more of rocks. we were in January the wave were not very high and water temperature was perfect.
title: one of the snorkelling destinations

body: We went here twice. Its a small beach, few turists and some locals. No food or other facilities, only a guy selling juice and cocktails, but still nice. Also you can do some snorkeling if you bring your own gear! You walk through "the jungle" to get here and may see monkeys, monitor Lizards, peacocks and maybe other animals on your hike.
title: Few turists and beautiful beach

body: Well what can I say this place is spectacular, the beach is absolutely beautiful, the cocktail bar serves wonderful drinks and if your into snorkelling it’s a great location.
title: Wonderful day at the beach

body: Took a 500 LKR Tuk Tuk from Unawatuna to jungle beach, and spent a lovely afternoon there (there are plenty of Tuk Tuks waiting there to take people back, no need to arrange a round trip). The walk down from the road is a mix of rocky stairs and dirt. We went on a Saturday, and the beach was packed with tourists and locals, but there was a patch of sand for everyone.
title: Worth a visit

body: Our friends had read and heard mixed reviews of this beach. We actually quite enjoyed it! The water was clear and lovely. We got a tuk tuk there and had a great time walking back to unawatuna beach. Would recommend visiting this beach. Perhaps don't bother snorkelling as there is not much to see.
title: Great beach

body: We explored by walking the area up to jungle beach. It was a cloudy day but the beach was surrounded by nice trees and flowers and very quiet. Around it seems to be larger villa resort but still I appreciated that the beach was not crowded. There a small rotti / juice shop on the beach. Nice beach if you want less waves and less people around.
title: Jungle secret besch

body: Worth going to the Jungle Beach - fantastic scenery, great water quality and lovely view. Absolute must - if you are nearby.
title: Great beach

body: You have to take a short downhill trek through the jungle to get to this beach, which was very enjoyable. The beach itself is nice to look at, but the water is not great for swimming. There are dead corals everywhere and chunks of rock you can injure yourself on. The water is muddy because a river empties into the ocean nearby.
title: Nice trek, disappointing beach

body: We walked from Unawatuna to the Junglebeach, a very nice but not very easy walk. The beach is beautiful, nice sand, clear water with beautiful fishes (snorkling). Unfortunatly it is very crowded, even visited by groups! You can also reach the beach by car now. So don't expect an idyllic quiet beach. Unfortunately there is a lot of junk (plastic bottles) behind the beach and in the jungle. We did't find any garbage cans. We think in a few years, there is not much left of this beach
title: Cristal clear water, nice sandy beach, to many people and junk.

body: This was a stunning little beach! It had a great cocktail bar and also a small place to eat which I didn’t try but it was great for snorkelling and the monkeys provided some great entertainment going about their business! It was great to sit back and relax and take in the beautiful surroundings!
title: Holiday

body: Small beach with a lot of waste, boats and people - no need to go there. There are better beaches in Sri Lanka. Disappointing
title: No need to go there

body: The owner of our place in Galle recommended we visit Jungle Beach early before the crowds, we got there at 08:30 and had to ourselves for about 30 mins before snorkel boats arrived and other people from down the track. We drove ourselves and parked by the shop for 100, we then walked down the track to the beach - you could take a tuk tuk all the way. Snorkelling just off the beach was good, hence the boats, and the sand is lovely - a sweet little beach between Unawatuna and Galle
title: Cute little beach, go early

body: The only problem is that we need to hire a tuk tuk to go down the hill about 1km to get to the beach, but the beach itself is very nice with crystal clear water. The beach is bit crowded with limited parking area.
title: Best and clean beach ever

body: Compared to the beach in unawatuna this one was heavily overcrowded. People said it would be much more chilled out than the other beaches, but this was not the case. The beach was clean and we could not see any trash in the water. The hike was nice and not strenous for young people. I’d advise to check it out, but not get your hopes up high.
title: Heavily overcrowded small beach

body: Perfect beach with a great tropical feeling. Not to crowded when w e were there. Sell water and beverages at the beach. Lion bear 500rupies, cola 300. Was offered tuktuk there for 200rupies from "no name resort". When you go back the first tuktuk are a bit sneaky and demands 600rupies for the return. We walk towards the pagoda(right turn) about 300m and got a return for 300rupies. Recommend snorkeling. Lots of fish and octopus.The walk there trough the jungle trail is quite warm and exhausting, you literary walk trough the jungle and there are steep climbs and descends. The walk is not for olds and probably not perfect for families. If i went there again it would definitely be tuktuk.
title: Perfect snorkeling, take tuktuk.

body: Different beach than Unawatuna. It is less crowdy, with a view on a rock cliff. Worth visiting at least once. Buy a coconut when going back to Unawatuna!
title: Fine beach

body: This beach is a little bit of a walk but you can get a tuk tuk to get there. I personally loved resting under palms and swimming in this calm bay. It’s quite popular so better go there in the morning to avoid crowds.
title: Nice beach

body: Seems to be a hidden germ, but it is not really that; quite a few people (local & tourists) use this place which has a nice atmosphere, but it is crowded and there are far better alternatives further East along the coast if you want more privacy.
title: nice beach, but a bit dirty.

body: The beach and area are beautiful. I think when you catch the beach at a quiet moment it will be amazing. When we visit jungle beach on poya day it was very crowded and lots of locals were getting drunk and partied at the beach.
title: Lovely beach

body: My favorite spot during our short trip of 4 days in Sri Lanka. The beach and the surroundings are really amazing and worth visiting!You can reach from Unawatuna beach road with Tuk Tuk for 350-400 rupieh. Then you walk down through the bushes to reach to the beach, which is an experience by itself! The sea is not wavy so it is very good for a swim. There is one local bar offering drinks and some food for good rates.
title: You should not miss this beach!

body: You need to walk down the hill about 1km to get to the beach, but the beach itself is very nice with shallow water. The only downside is that it is a bit too crowded. There is only limited parking space on the roadsides, but there are private parking spaces - although their charges are somewhat unreasonable.
title: Well worth the walk down the hill

body: A nice walk through the jungle ruined by the beach which is very polluted and full of stacked up rubbish . Swimming is also difficult with coral and rocks underfoot . Don’t get what the fuss is about
title: Dirty beach

body: Nice but a bit crowded beach, the view over Galle is not super nice but the hike was kind of fun. Visit the temple nearby as well
title: Nice beach

body: Jungle beach was a disappointment. Walk to beach enjoyable, shaded by the trees, while the monkeys play. Steep hill with a poor footpath. Beach was very narrow, don’t really think you can say it has a restaurant, I certainly wouldn’t of eaten there. Sea polluted with plastic. Sold to us as a good place to snorkel with no waves, we never saw one fish only litter.
title: Polluted and dirty

body: The trek to the beach was fairly enjoyable but this was in no way a secret. The beach was heaving and there was rubbish everywhere. Snorkelling trips were regular but all the coral has died in the area so there is nothing to see in the water.
title: Busy With Loads of Rubbish

body: I visited Jungle Beach on two occasions - one walking from Unawatuna through the "jungle" and another time via tuk tuk. The walk from Unawatuna was awesome through the bush and added to the specialness of arriving at the beach. This would not be suited for anyone with difficulty walking due to the stairs and uneven surfaces. If you do this walk it is doable in flip flops. The trip by tuk tuk was quick. There are two beaches - accessible to each other across some rocks. Well worth visiting both. The beach is lovely and less people than on the beaches at Unawatuna. Be careful when you enter the water as there are many rocks in areas which are not clearly visible until you step onto them. Look for where others are swimming and go to those areas. Lovely beach with no wind. Must visit.
title: Gorgeous Beach - lovely walk through the bush to get there

body: This beach had ace reviews so it was high on my list. Firstly it's not for people who aren't particularly mobile as you have to walk down a steep slope/hillside to get there. The water had plastic in it so not the cleanest beach or water. There are hidden rocks/coral along much of it. Swim where there are people, if there is a section with no one there, prob due to hidden rocks under the water. There are much nicer beaches than here.
title: Disappointing

body: the beach like a out door pool. really nice. also we have try snorkeling. worth money. Rs.1500 for locals.
title: really nice beach like a pool

body: Went in the afternoon... Crowded, a lot of rubbish on the sand. Would be a nice spot if they cleaned it up.Nice walk down through the jungle.Can walk to it from Unawatuna
title: Not great

body: We got there at 8am and were first on the beach to get our pick of sun loungers.Sun rises from behind beach, and is on the beach from about 9.It’s a small beach but nice to walk along. Quite a bit of litter washing up & quite a few rocks in the water.Still nice to see and spend a few hours.
title: Morning visit

body: Water was filled with garbage at our visit.Otherwise a very beautiful beach.The access is a bit of a hike.
title: Looks nice but filthy water

body: The walk through the woods is quiet fun and to add to that the Beautiful jingle beach!! The water was a bit rough so we couldn't snorkel or do any water activities but a great place to just lay down on the beach bed and enjoy the view :)
title: Beautiful Beach!

body: The beach could be beautiful with nice sand and green hills leading down to it. But both the water and the beach is full of plastic garbage. When you snorkel it is easier to spot a coke can than a fish. When you swim a bit further out you can see quite a lot of fish though.
title: Beach full of garbage

body: Small beach without tourists or almost. Guaranteed immersion. This beach is worth, you have to walk a little, hence its name.
title: Local experience

body: We walked there today and it was really busy! I wouldn’t say that’s there much charm or appeal about either of the bays of Jungle Beach as they’re both surrounded by rubbish, the sea is quite murky and there’s a restaurant which has a monopoly so they charge a lot for food. The path between the two beaches was pretty waterlogged, with a thick smelly mud. We both almost lost a flip flop to it and ended up with black mud up our legs and clothes. Grim.
title: Very busy and not clean

body: The hike to the beach is lovely. We saw leguaans, butterflies and snakes. However, the beach itself is nothing special. It’s secluded but not that nice. Also, the beach faces the city of Galle with its industrial buildings and hotels, which isn’t a very pretty view. It is worth going there on a hike, but I would recommend the nearby Unawatuna beach for sunbathing etc.
title: Nothing special about the beach - nice hike though

body: Nothing special. I've seen much better beaches.Pros: sand, secluded place.Cons: far away, no sunbeds, a lot of plastic trash around.
title: Nothing special

body: Good spot for snorkelling (we saw many fish but the best was the cuttle fish). Lots of monkeys in the trees on the beach and iguanas as well.
title: A real jungle beach, very natural and quite small

body: I went to the jungle beach on a snorkeling trip. I'm not sure whether it was due to a recent storm, but visibility wasn't that great...and there was a lot of rubbish in the water.A nice enough stretch of beach for an afternoons sun worshipping.
title: Nice beach, but quite a bit of rubbish in the sea when snorkeling

body: Nice walk down the the beach but an anticlimax when you reach it. Unfortunately it’s littered with plastic bottles otherwise it would be beautiful.
title: Nice walk, but littered beach

body: Lovely walk, quite beach, surrounded by wildlife, monkeys and large lizards, snorkelling and chilling
title: Well worth the ramble

body: We went here for snorkling, the beach was really polluted and there were a lot of people. Not recommended for relaxation. Ok for snorkling.
title: Plastic everywhere and crowded!

body: Visited here for the day, it could be amazing but unfortunately the sea is full of rubbish (I guess due to the bay) so all pretty disgusting. Ended up back at Unawatuna where there is no rubbish
title: A dirty side of paradise

body: The inclusion of this beach in Lonely Planet means lots of folks know about it, but that does make it less lovely. You have to sort of hike down to it and the beach feels very secluded. Great.
title: Not a Secret but Fun

body: We read some mixed reviews about this beach. We tried anyway, and even though our expectations were not very high, we still got a bit disappointed.You will find a steep slope with some man made steps, not in the best of conditions, but still easy to access the beach. There was a lot of garbage in the path of "jungle".The beach was also super dirty, and you can see that this garbage comes from the sea, with the tide bringing bottles, plastics and other stuff. The sand is mostly coral rock, so, not very comfortable.Small in sand area, with many local small boats, and a few "bars" it's hard to find a place to put your towel.I would recommend to skip this one.
title: Not that impressive

body: I'm sure this was a secluded tranquil beach about 15 years ago. It was packed when we got there with very little beach to sit on. Pretty but not quite as peaceful as we'd hoped!
title: Busy, not so secret beach!

body: Not the best beach. Small, trash in water and on beach and if you are unlucky (as we are) there are groups of screaming local youngsters playing loud music. Beach in Unawatuna is better.
title: Not the best. Stay in Unawatuna

body: Yes it's nice but it was very filthy with rubbish and it's very small. Not my favourite place to visit in Sri Lanka that's for sure.
title: Not worth the hype

body: I walked from the peace pagoda to the jungle beach which was a nice 10-15min walk but the beach itself is dirty and was very full in the afternoon.
title: Dirty and full

body: Pros:- Clean beach- Not too crowded - Calm sea- Access to White Jungle Beach among the rocks / path (Personally I preferred Jungle Beach)Cons:- Be aware 30min walk through the wilderness (unless getting a Tuc-Tuc to a local Hotel)
title: Beach

body: Just lovely! Fairly quiet, not too touristy, right in the middle of a jungle with real monkies;) You'll be able to get all refreshments and fruits. Mind you the path down to the beach is still a bit wild, true Sri Lankan experience!
title: November beach day

body: A short walk through the jungle if you go by tuk-tuk. Otherwise a bit longer from the main road. There are two beaches with some rocks in between. You have to scramble over the rocks to go between them. There are quite some fish just in front of these rocks so very nice snorkeling straight from the beach. There are some guys with boats to take you further out, but I don’t know what they charge or if it is worth it to go further out. Gets busier after 11:00. When we were there, both beaches were free of rubbish.
title: Nice little beach for snorkeling

body: Nice place to relax. The beach strip isn't too long but it's long enough and not many people are aware of the place.There is a little bar with seats for a refreshment at normal pricing. If you don't mind taking the short hike down the road through the woods, def a nice place to relax and have a fresh juice.
title: Not too crowded beach

body: Small Beach used by locals. Food available and Beer. Prices resonable. Water calm and warm. 500r from town with Tuc Tuc. Spent a nice afternoon there away from the hustle and bustle of City.
title: Natural Beauty

body: We walked from Unawatuna - takes about 30 minutes through a nice jungle track.Unfortunately the beach itself is strewn with rubbish - in the jungle, on the sand and in the water. Ruins an otherwise nice, calm spot to swim.
title: Nice beach ruined by rubbish

body: We heard this was an amazing beach but were sadly disappointed. Way overcrowded with gangs of teenage boys banging on their drums. Rubbish everywhere and the water looked brown. Beach hut way overpriced and staff extremely rude. Go to another beach and save yourself the time!
title: Rude staff and garbage everywhere

body: Lovely days spent in this hidden treasure! Perfect for young kids and snorkeling. Good way to spend the day and maybe go to the next beach on for the late afternoon surfing!
title: Great for kids

body: Can hike to this beach through a trail in the jungle in about 20-30 minutes from the beach near Unawatuna. Saw some monkeys swinging through the trees. Not totally secluded but still special.
title: Nice beach away from the crowd

body: The guys who managed to put up a beach hut acts as if he owns the beach. He make sure he exploits every opportunity to the maximum. The outrageous amounts he charges cannot be justified by the way he maintains the beach area. I know its not his duty, But he could at least do something about the huge pile of garbage that is collecting at the beach. I'm sure he is a major contributor to it.
title: Exploitation at its best!!!

body: Tiny strip of sand between a steep jungle covered slope and a dirty sea. Took a glass bottom boat and the bay, saw plenty of plastic bags and bottles float passed but only about three fish. Really wouldn't bother!
title: Don't know what all the fuss is about

body: You get here by walking downhill a few hundred meters on a path through the jungle. Actually 2 beaches. Some parts has a lot of trash and nobody cleans.Visited during October and before the weather settled. Less waves here than on Unawatuna and other beaches further east.Tip: we visited on a weekend, and the beach was very crowded. In addition a large group of young boys spent the day there getting drunk. Probably not a problem unless you travel with kids or are looking for a quiet getaway
title: Nice walk through the jungle, but very crowded in the weekend

body: We went early in the morning and no one was there. It was a perfect time for a swim. The walk was beautiful through the forest where we came across monkeys and lovely colourful birds.
title: A nice place for a quiet swim

body: It is unusual to go to the beach through a jungle, but it is good experience. The sand is pleasant for feet, the sunset is great as well, yet once we were in the water, there are rests of shells etc. and I scratched myself to blood when a wave hit me down.. therefore 4/5.. the waves are generally bigger in this part of Sri Lanka, so it is nice to watch, but not so great to swim in.. in the afternoon.. the best option is to come in the morning:)
title: a beach in the real jungle :)

body: No longer a hidden location, Nice beach for a swim. Foreigners and locals as well. May be 90% locals, lot of noise coming from shouting, drumming, dancing and just having fun. All seem to get alone fine. Bit of trash thrown around but surprised not too much. There are two beaches – we were at the far end one. Few parking spots available. Was getting busier as we left around 11 AM..
title: No longer a hidden location, Nice beach for a swim.

body: Breath taking experience! Very pristine beach with soft sand and clear water. The walk to get here maybe tiresome and little scary especially in the evening but definitely worth the trouble.
title: A real treat

body: We were directed to this place by a friend. The tuk tuk driver knew where to take us and directed us to a path that leads down to the beach. We managed to negotiate the off beaten path in flip flops but it is uneven in places so do take care. This beach was beautiful once at the bottom, not overcrowded and seemed to be a favourite among the locals. There is a small cafe type bar on the beach serving drinks and light bites. The sea is calm enough to swim around here, walking to the left over the rocks you'll get to another cove which seems a lot cleaner than the first.
title: Little gem of a find

body: This is a decent beach on Rumasulla Mountain that you can cover along with Japanese peace pagoda. More untouched and less commercial. None of the restaurants were open when we went, probably because there were very few tourists. It's a 5 minute walk from the main road through the jungle. You can get your picnic basket and drinks and spend half a day here.
title: Decent Beach with no activities during off seaosn

body: This beach is popular among the tourists and locals. Great place to hang around for one or two hours. It is located inside a jungle. You have to hike down for 5 minutes before reaching the beach! Food and drinks at the Jungle beach is expensive.
title: Isolated beach!

body: Nice little beach, not very busy and just one drinks vendor. Also if you're there at the right time of day the sunset is amazing.
title: Nicely isolated

body: This beach is a Tuk tuk ride away from Unawatuna beach. It was ok, but quite a walk down, which then means quite a walk back up. There was a bar and food available. Wouldnt go back, but glad we visited.
title: Great beach, but quite a trek downhill

body: This place was just down the beach from the Riu Sri Lanka.A lovely little place on the beach, we enjoyed a candle light dinner.The food was fantastic, if you like medium spice the devilled chicken is amazing, the pasta dishes are equally good.Returned today for a massage, again great treatment and really friendly happy staff. Well well worth a visit if you're in the area.Thanks guys Phil & lisa
title: Dinner and massage

body: Sounds exotic till you get there. The walk up and down to the beach, if you chose to walk is fairly easy. Remember to carry water with you. Stay hydrated. The beach was full of families and kids making a lot of noise. If you want to avoid the crowd follow a few almost obscure trails you will find in the way. The will take you to some secluded spots with amazing views.
title: Not as secluded as it sounds

body: It's a beautiful bay where mostly locals come. Normally you can go snorkeling there, but when we were there the waves were a bit too rough. Also, the people just throw all their trash between the trees..
title: Nice among the locals

body: a nice beach with a charming trek down the mountain. a good spot relax and enjoy the water and weather. the bar also serves some good drinks and food
title: a nice beach with a charming trek down the mountain.

body: Visited this cute sheltered beach on a Saturday in August and just loved the vibe here!Would not put it in the " best beaches in the world " category- but definitely worth a look.The beach was full of local families laughing and having fun ,and groups of young guys in groups signing and drumming what sounded like Sri Lankan rap!I read a review on this beach mentioning that in the weekends it has too many locals ( gosh,when did travellers /tourists become so narcissistic???).You are in Sri Lanka..Hello!For me this made the whole beach even better- and as a solo female,did not at all feel at any time worried.
title: Great vibe !

body: There are 2 parts to the beach... visiting the smaller one is a must! If you look on the internet for images of the beach, they will not capture the beauty of it! The best view is paddled slightly out to sea and looking back where you can see the beautiful pagoda in the background. A must see!!
title: Most beautiful beach I've ever seen

body: Perhaps this place is too well known and advertised, it's far from being a secluded romantic private beach. It's not worth a visit. The sea is not altogether clean, prices at the bar on one of the small beaches are inflated. if this is your only coastal stop travel round further east to Weligama.
title: Busy and dirty

body: There are far better and cleaner beaches nearby(unawantuna), not advisable to go all the way.The beach is crowded and small.
title: Smal, crowded beach

body: If you want to go to a smaller beach with locals, you have to go here. It's a little bit noisy, but if you go when there are no holidays it's pretty quite I think. There is one bar at one side of jungle beach, the other small beach doesn't have a bar or restaurant.
title: Small and lot of locals

body: The beach felt adventurous to get to walking through the jungle, there was a very expensive bar there, if you head down the beach to the left and between the rocks and carry on over the other rocks you get to a much nicer beach. Tuk tuks can also get you to this side of jungle beach. It is well worth the short walk up to the Japanese peace pagoda
title: A nice enough beach

body: Getting to this beach will cost you 300 one way from anywhere in Unawatuna in a tuk tuk.The prices for food and beverage at the little market at the entrance will charge more than MRP because they take advantage of all the tourists coming in. Better to bring your own food and waterThe beach was pretty... But this month of August, the waves were too big for swimming and there were too many rocks and coral pieces all around for comfort. The coral pieces are all along the beach, which makes for a nice thing to look at but bad for walking on sand. Not soft sand.Not a good swimming beach. I went in and the waves crashed me down and my foot hit a rock. Got some big scratches.There's a few places there to order drinks and food, but are bloody expensive. The benefit is that there are chairs to sit and lounge on.Wouldn't come back to this beach.
title: Too many corals

body: This serene beach is surrounded by a strip of vegetation and rock formations. There is a 5min hike through a jungle area where at the end we are presented with this mesmerizing beach.
title: " Paradise on Earth"

body: We came here in the morning in the second week of July. There were few other people around and so it was not crowded. We saw several large monitor lizards. The water was calm and refreshing for swimming. We took a tuk tuk to the top of the hill and hiked down from what the driver called the "tourist entrance" which came out at the little restaurant. Then we went to the left of the restaurant over some rocks to a little cove to swim. We did not find this area dirty. There was a path up the hill from this area to the pagoda where we caught another tuk tuk back to our villa.
title: nice swimming in July

body: Very small beach with a lot of rubbish on the sand - even a needle!! Only one eating place on the beach.
title: Small and dirty beach

body: This is a nice sheltered cove that avoids the pounding from the big rolling waves of the Indian Ocean. There's not a lot in terms of facilities but there is good natural shade and safe bathing. Makes a nice place for a day if you are in the area although coach loads of tourists turning up for a quick gawp does take the shine off it
title: A small protected beach just around the corner from Unawatuna

body: Need to trek down the hill a bit to get to this beach but the views are worth it. Can be difficult for small children and elders. Beach does get crowded a bit.
title: Not so hidden beaxh

body: I've heard of Jungle Beach, the secluded stretch of beach just west of Unawatuna, for awhile now. I eventually made my way one afternoon and couldn't help feel a bit uncomfortable. In the offseason, there's fewer tourists everywhere and being 1 of only 3 other tourists after walking down a long jungle path to the beach was a bit eerie. Staff were eager and the water was not as clean since it's now in the bay with the Galle harbour. If you're visiting from April to October, best just stay on the Unawatuna main beach area. It's much nicer anyway.
title: Eerie in the off-season

body: I liked this place, just the small road to the beach..you need to walk there carefully. The waves there was pretty big and it is getting deep very fast. Anyway it is beautiful place where to take rest and seems that that place atract those who like to play some music instrument. During my stay there 2 big groups of people came and were playing music instruments..so it made the place look even better.
title: Place where to take a rest

body: It takes some effort to reach Jungle beach but it is an amazing experience down there. Sea is calm in the morning and as you swim, you will get to see amazing views. There is a small stall where you can buy refreshments and snacks. Just bring your towel and some change, you will be good to go.
title: A hidden gem

body: This is a secluded beach front remote to Galle. To reach there, half of the way you can hire a Tuk Tuk, next half you have to trek though forest pathway. Place is good for swimming and snorkeling as well.
title: Ideal For Relaxing

body: It's a private beach and a mini trek to get there. Recommend going there in the morning or before 6:00 pm as the jungle to get there has no lights in the evening. If it's dark while returning, I suggest the traveller to carry a torch light. A must visit while you are staying in and around Cantaloupe Levels and surrounding resorts.
title: Pristine Private Beach

body: Too much PR of this place but as for me nothing special . Just nice beach but not more then this . U can try 1-2 times . To go there cost like 200 rubies on tuktuk. Ask discount usualy they Agree for 200..
title: Normal

body: I had to do some figuring before I could reach this place. My tuk-tuk driver was not aware of this beach so I used google maps to finally reach there.I visited this place in early morning. The trail is easy but full of garbage. It’s not often you get to wander a empty beach. The waves were crawling gently to the shore. There was only one empty boat in the sea which completed the view. One can smell the fresh air of ocean.Its best to avoid this place after weekend parties as garbage compiles up. Also this it gets over crowded easily as it is a small beach. Best time to visit is early morning.
title: Secluded and serene beach

body: Worth the little walk to find the place! There are actually two beaches connected and both are worth checking out. I loved that it was less tourist oriented and there were lots of locals hanging around. Such a lovely little oasis.
title: Our favourite beach in Sri Lanka

body: We were there on the low season. Quiet place, some bars to get fresh fruit juices or cocktails. But I even preferred the way before the beach, to reach it, in the middle of the jungle with the possibility to see monkeys. We saw two.
title: Quiet place

body: Place is quite remote. It'stake some time to get there. There is bit of climbing to get there and back. At the time of visit there was no restaurant on the beach. Just a couple guys selling coconuts, water and beer. Have a feeling place become popular and bit overcrowded at middle of the day.
title: Good spot to enjoy sun and ocean

body: Delicious food and coctails, very reasonably priced. Nice and friendly staff.Lovely unspoilt beach, soft white sands and very clean, sea was clean and clear. Highly recommend
title: Cozy restaurant and beautiful beach

body: Lonely Planet says it's a hidden pearl that everyone knows about, and it's a pearle indeed. When we were there, it was still quiet, and that's what it should stay.
title: Indeed a hidden paradise!

body: Jungle beach is small and a small trek away from Unawatuna but worth the effort. We walked along the path from Unawatuna visited the Japonese Peace Pagoda and then on to Jungle beach. Jungle Beach is smaller than expected but picturesque and great for snorkelling or swimming or just a nice place to relax. The waves are small and a walk into the sea is nice and easy. Take a picnic and your camera and you won't regret it.
title: A beach to relax

body: great place to experience a touch of wilderness with close proximity to the ancient city of Galle A 15 minute climb down a Forrest pathway will lead you to a beach secluded from the the hustle and bustle Ideal location to relaxcaution: there is no lifeguards so you are on your own..
title: breathtaking, beautiful, touch of wilderness and serenity

body: Amazing clean beach with comfy sand! Jungle beach is in a bay so there are no huge waves. At the beach you can find sunbeds and bar with cold drinks and snacks.
title: Amazing beach

body: Disapointed! Dirty beach and water. I just say one thing. Dont bother go here. Go to Unawatuna beach instead.
title: Not as beautiful as they say!

body: This place is unreal. It is a postcard beach. Hidden through a steep jungle entrance you can enjoy a day basking in the sun and snorkelling in the sea. (ask the tuk tuk driver to take you to the entrance by the Japanese peace pagoda, its more the locals beach so less people) simply delightful. 1 person selling drinks. Take food with you or up the hill is a few places to eat.
title: The beach postcards are made on!

body: Paradise beach! No constructio only trees. In the middle of the jungle. Really quiet sea and calm beach.
title: Paradise

body: If you are visiting Galle, this is a beach that you should not miss. This beach is usually not crowded as the Unawatuna beach. Ideal location to have a swim in the sea. There aren't any beach restaurants available at the site but parking facilities, few shops and places to have a shower are available near-by. Please make sure you don't litter in the beach. This is a clean beach comparing to some other beaches around. You also can have a visit to the temple nearby which offers some great views of the Galle city and the sea.
title: Best beach in Galle

body: Beautiful place to be at, theres no much to do around or in there but to enjoy the precious view of the jungle.
title: Beautiful

body: Beautiful place still but shame it has been found. Was pleased to see that I was bein cleaned of rubbish when we were there as this is obviously a problem.
title: An insight into what it would have been like to find this place before tourism

body: It is a very small beach accessible from the peace pagoda. A walk of 10 minutes downhill. Nice to see if u go to pace pagoda
title: Small secluded beach

body: We walked to Jungle Beach from Unawatuna based on the Trip Advisor reviews. It's a very sweaty arduous walk on a very poor trail. When we finally got there it was a complete anti climax. The beach is small, unremarkable and overcrowded. It's a good hour of my life I will never get back! Skip it - you're not missing a thing.
title: Biggest anti climax ever!

body: Really nice beach but weird local guy was following me some of the way and randomly asked me is I wanted to have sex with him. I got out of the situation well but it got me scared since I was on my own.
title: Really nice!

body: Nice beach. Would be rather happy if the water was more cleaner. Once we stepped in to water, there were lots of polythene bags and dirty stuff which fouled our legs. Environment was so beautiful. Be careful if you are going with kids as the tides are little stronger.
title: Nice Beach

body: Central part of the beach is okay and has a nice bar, however rest of the beach is covered in rubbish and we met a girl who got her stuff stolen. Nice jungle hike up to the beach. If interested visit but be carefull and keep your expectations low.
title: Messy

body: Ifv you want a day away from the bustle of Unawatuna, this is the palce to escape to just around the bay from Una. A secluded beach that is easilly accessible by boat and to have a BBQ fish lunch and fantastic day out.
title: Selcuded beach

body: Not a bad place to go with your mates and have a cold beer.only downfall is that this place is very dirty .polythene bags and plastic bottles were all over the place .if someone could clean this up that'd be great.and cmon guys please don't litter this place.its a gem of a place !!
title: Chilled place

body: This place is a bit off the main road, you can google it for the directions so it was easy to find. You have to walk down the hill to get to the beach and first the path was a bit rocky but half way there was some steps to go down. We went there around 5 in the evening and most of the people were going back at that time so the beach was fairly empty with just few locals and foreigners. Which was great because we were able to enjoy the beach leisurely. But I heard from a local that the previous week it was packed up and there was a huge traffic.We had the chance to see the beautiful sunset which was amazing. Overall it was a great experience but wish there was some changing rooms so that we could easily change clothes.
title: Beautiful Sunset!

body: Wouldn't recommend this beach, the water feels "dirty", the beach is crowded with locals which is fine, except that the local women can only get into the ocean with clothes on, so the few tourists in bikini are starred at. It's nice with all the green surroundings, but not the beach I prefer
title: Why go here?

body: If they cleaned it up it would be a definite 5Would have been a beautiful walk through jungle if it wasn't for the small piles of rubbish along route and the bits of rubbish on sand and rocks. It could be amazing
title: Rubbish in Paradise

body: Jungle beach is about 1,5 km from Unawatuna beach, you can walk or take a tub-tuk. It is definitely the best beach for swimming, quiet and lovely water. There are two Jungle beaches, the first is small, but also the nicest. The other is bigger. Very crowded on week ends and holidays.Bring your own food and water, there are pedlars who sell seafood, but don't count on it.
title: Hidden gem

body: Could be a beautiful beach with a nice view to Galle, but it's full of rubish. We needed to walk in the jungle, which was interesting but not worth it if you are planning to swim. Disappointing 😕
title: Dirty!

body: This beach is beautiful, but takes a little bit of getting to for those who are not the most mobile. For those able to scramble along a jungle path, they are rewarded with a wonderful, peaceful beach, with gentle waves and great snorkeling potential.
title: Gorgeous beach, paradise-like

body: It isn't worth to go there, especially for beaching or swimming. Very small and DIRTY. I won't never go there anymore
title: Laying in the sun

body: A Beach , Surrounded by jungle. I have visited few times. and some times back there was no any shops or seller mens on the beach.That was very beautiful. Need to careful while bathing on sea. Because it is SEA. Still the beach is in clear condition and we need to be careful not to litter.
title: Only in Unawatuna

body: I belive that idea of jungle beach was good but nobody took care about this place. It's very small area which looks like garbage dump. Absolutely not worth to see.
title: Garbage dump

body: The long trek to this beach is not worth one's while! It is a busy beach frequented by the locals with a few tourists. People are bathing fully clothed.Security is an issue.
title: Long Jungle trek! Dirty Beach

body: Beautiful nice clear water. Coke 300 rupees but hey it was cold and glad I didnt have to lug stuff up and down that hill. 500 rupees for a tuk tuk there and same approx back. Quite a steep hill from where you are dropped at the top of the hill - and of course if you go down you need to go back up! Cocktails available and food (but I didn't try. Loungers available I think covered by purchasing drinks. Take sunscreen and plan to spend a few hours.
title: Worth the walk (about 5 mins down hill) and 7 mins back up

body: Great beach. Beautiful view. Clean and secluded. Bit tricky to get to and from. Would visit again. Can spend the day there relaxing easily.
title: Exploring

body: Love the beach, there is shadow from the plants. Many monkeys hanging around ! You can reach by foot 20 min away from Unawatuna cross the jungle. Many tourists go on the small path. Amazing experience !
title: Very nice wild place

body: Set on the small coast at the beginning of Unawatuna, this spot is a great swimming zone with good fun people. We also took a catamaran Cruise that set sail from here. Very pleasant. Recommended!
title: A landscape to remember

body: Nice, but you need to be able to get there ... steps or a bit of climbing ... but the reward is exceptional.
title: Nice and quiet ... a small part and a separated large part.

body: Really good beach. It was a little dirty once because there was alot of plastic trash in the water. But the next time I visti it was clear water with nice fish to see. Nice to see!
title: Very nice Beach.

body: Friends recommended this place but it was nothing special at all . The beach is quite small and there is lots of dirt swept under the bushes. We went once only .
title: Not impressed

body: Really small but beautiful beach. Frequented by locals and tourists alike. Calm, clean water. To access it, you'll have to go up a hill (via tuk-tuk/car), and then walk down an easy 'jungle' path.
title: Cute little beach

body: Dont bother. Small, crowded, polluted water with trash floating around. Wouldnt even consider swimming here.
title: Filthy

body: The most overrated spot on the Beach. After walking a long Walk from Unawatuna We came to this little Beach. To Many people.
title: Overrated

body: Go early! The walk there is lovely and well sign posted.The beach is small, but beautiful. There are shady spots too. The water is stunning and quiet, no waves.
title: Amazing, beautiful and peaceful

body: This is an especially good destination if you're staying on Unawatuna Beach. The jungle walk to Jungle Beach is charming and rewarded with snack bars on the way. Much gentler beach than the big surf at Unawatuna
title: Great hidden beach

body: We went to snorkel however the water wasn't clear enough to see anything. The beach is cute but small in the little cove we went to but it didn't offer much.
title: Jungle beach

body: I advise walking down to get the full experience (it only takes 15 minutes) but this is a lovely little hideaway with gentler currents than elsewhere in the bay. A bit of rubbish floating round but the water itself and beach were clean.
title: Lovely beach used by locals

body: The beach has the potential to be beautiful, unfortunately there is quite a lot of litter that gathers near the trees so you're unable to sit in the shade that they provide. The walk down wasn't for the weak but we stopped and admired the monkeys playing in the trees and posing for the cameras. It is a nice beach but if you're planning on making quite a journey to it I wouldn't suggest you do. However if you're close I don't see why you shouldn't go for a few hours.
title: Few drawbacks

body: I had the really nice walk from Unawatuna to get here.The beach is nice but small and get crowded quickly. I went here on a thursday morning... Arriving there another 5 was already on the beach and 30 min later a Schoolclass and a couple doing there weddingphotography with a crew of 10 made the beach less serene. Actually Unawatuna beach is less crowded 😂I might have been just unlucky - the place is nice so well worth a visit.
title: Beautiful but not that secluded

body: At jungle beach you really have to earn your swim with a hike up the hill and down the forest path to the beach.And what a swim it is! I love that the water is so calm that it's actually possible to swim quite far out to sea, which is rare in this area.Nice, shady trees, sun loungers some picturesque boats dotted around as well as lunch facilities make this a truly great beach.It's perfect to round off the beach time with another short hike to Unawatuna.
title: My favourite Beach in the area

body: Lovely beach to wander down to if you have time. It's small and we went at sun set and it was fairly quiet and a lovely spot to see the sunset from. We walked from Unawatuna beach, up to the peace pagoda, and then down to Jungle Beach. Was a fun little afternoon adventure.
title: Cute beach

body: Spent here half a day and whilst it is a nice beach in terms of landscape and an area with clear water / rocks / corals to snorkel, the shore is truly dirty and full of rubbish (bottles, food packages etc.) There is not much shade either and to get there, you have to go up a hill - not too bad, just bear in mind the heat!
title: Nice but really dirty

body: The beach is no longer a secret and while it is pleasant enough the water was a bit murky and the coral has been trashed. We walked there from Unawatuna in half an hour but tuk-tuk is an alternative. We only stayed a couple of hours since it was a Saturday and was beginning to get crowded. There are better beaches in Sri Lanka such as Mirissa.
title: Pleasant beach

body: We loved this beach. You take a tuktuk from town. Walk down to the beach about 10 minutes and you have a gorgeous secluded beach with a little restaurant. Great for swimming, lounge chairs and have a restaurant open until 5pm. Great view across the bay to Galle fort. We have already returned again. Go visit it's worth it
title: A great getaway beach in the town

body: Jungle Beach is small, but beautiful. There are beach loungers to use. There are restaurants that serve food and drinks. This beach is a great place to spend an afternoon!
title: Beautiful beach

body: this is a nice beach in down south sri lanka good for relaxing and reading we stay over 3 days in this beach swim and diving prefect activities @ here
title: nice beach but more people

body: It's about a big beach erea divided between sands and rocks with calm ( low waves) waters surrounded by jungle trees and a nearby Buddhist temple.
title: Nice sandy & rocky beach

body: Jungle Beach is not very far from Unawatuna (just a bus ride away if you're taking local transport - you can also walk if you're up for it). It's very secluded. You have to climb down a hill to access it. In 2016 there was only restaurant serving food at the beach and was overpriced. The food was just average. It's a virgin beach. Go there to get away from the crowds.
title: Beautiful beach, calm and secluded

body: Had a great time there. Waves aren't rough so had no problems to swim. Safe beach as well. The outside areas have been corrupted by tourists with rubbish hence its not clean. But a good place to go for a swim and relax.
title: Beautifully beach and clear water

body: This can be termed as one of the virgin beaches of Ceylon and a beautiful location and a real gift of nature
title: Highly Scenic

body: great place to swim and hang out with the locals. you do have to climb down a hill to get access to the beach
title: hang out where the locals hang
Garbage & Theft
body: My experience here was awful. Lot's of garbage. You could fill 20 large rubbish bags easily. Theft. Met a tourist who caught Sri Lankans trying to steal $80 USD out of his wallet. They'll try and be your friend and distract you for n hour or so while their other friends find an oppurtunity to go through your belongings. You've been warned.

title: Romantic beach
body: Nice for picnic and snorkeling. Only 30 minutes walk from the lovely Simon's House you go through shadow little lane to this wonderful little beach!

title: Decent
body: Supposedly 'hidden' beach, at the end of a v heavily wooded, rocky downhill trail. Heavy with tourists when we went. Good bar serving drinks and food. Be careful with belongings though: a couple had their money (not the wallets, just the cash) stolen while in the water.

title: Dissapointed ...
body: Visited 1st time this beach 2 years ago in March 2015 and that was a very good experience with positive feelings. So today we were there with the expectations that if it will not be better at least it will be the same beach. But ... its a disaster. Its only my opinion but I'm writing now about my feelings. The water was dirty with some stinky smell. The beach itself its smaller than it used to be. 3 times smaller area. The place is dirty. The little cafe that was there its gone. Some strange people walking around. The beds on which we used to take a nap ;) are gone. The only good thing that is left its the view onthe jungles from water.

title: Overrated beach
body: We walked to the beach, scrambling over rocks, having been told it was worth visiting. The sand is good, but it is a narrow strip of land, with hard beds and a poor cafe. Better to stay in Unawatuna beach where the facilities are better.

title: Nice beach with a tropical feel
body: It's a nice beach but there's a fairly off the beaten track journey to get too the beech. Plenty of sandbag steps to negotiate. Once down on the beach it's fairly small and surrounded by nice scenery, the beech is used for partying in the evenings so it can be a little noisy / busy especially at the weekend. Very nice if you get your timings right !!

title: Nice beach close to Galle
body: We took a TukTuk from Galle to this hideaway which is located between Galle and Unawatuna. We paid around 400 Rupies from the fort.Don't expect a total secret place, but a nice beach with a bar, sunbeds and less people than in Unawatuna.Pro:+ close to Galle (you can see the lighthouse from there)+ small beach without mass tourism, but convenience like sunbeds and one restaurant with food and drinks+ ever Wednesday a beach party during night, probably just in high season+ almost no wavesCon:- sunbeds without mattress - some parts of the beach have stones in the water- some locals don't keep it 100% cleanPlease mark helpful if you like the review. Thanks.

title: very beautiful, good for snorkeling
body: Very beautiful place, a lot of monkeys on the way to the beach. The water is very clean, there are not so many people there.

title: This was our Blue Lagoon in good old days
body: Do you remember <The Blue lagoon >( Brooke Shields 1980)well this was our secrect Blue lagoon in late 70s and early 80s. so beautiful and unspoilt.it still has that charm to some extent but not lonely and deserted any more.but compared to a packed Unawatuna beach just other side of the Rumassla mountain which seperates strip, this is a breather

title: Okay beach
body: Nothing special about this beach. It's ouy of the main road, so not that crowded. However its quite small and not that nice. Hikkaduwa us better.
